articles.title: ‘What more do you want?’: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia’s blunt message on Rohit Sharma amid 2027 World Cup speculation
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has pushed back against growing speculation over Rohit Sharma's ODI future, insisting that the former India c.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has pushed back against growing speculation over Rohit Sharma's ODI future, insisting that the former India captain is continuing to perform at a high level and questioning why his place in the side is being debated.Speaking after a high-level Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) review meeting in Mumbai on Thursday, Saikia offered a firm defence of the 39-year-old, whose future has again become a major talking point with the 2027 ODI World Cup approaching.“He is playing superbly in all the matches. So, what more do you want? In the last match, he scored 138 runs. So, why there is a speculation? So, I don't want to give fodder to the speculations,” Saikia said.His comments came amid reports that selectors had considered moving on from Rohit in their ODI plans, potentially leaving his participation in the 2027 World Cup in doubt.Rohit answered speculation with Lord's centuryThe speculation intensified during India's ODI tour of England earlier this year, with reports suggesting the Lord's ODI could be Rohit's final appearance in an India shirt.Instead, Rohit responded in characteristic fashion — with a match-defining performance.He smashed 138 at Lord's, becoming the oldest Indian to score an ODI century at the iconic venue, although his effort came in a losing cause. The innings once again demonstrated why questions over his future have been accompanied by equally strong arguments for his retention.Following the England tour, Rohit made it clear that the constant speculation did not concern him.“If there's no noise, there's no fun. My job is inside; their job is outside. That's how I look at it,” he had said. “The noise since I made my debut was there. And till the time I'm going to stay here, it's always going to be there. It doesn't really matter too much. What matters is what I do on the field. I want to try and contribute to the success of the team. That's all my focus is.”Rohit retired from Test cricket in 2025 and from T20Is in 2024, leaving ODI cricket as his only remaining international format.The latest comments from Saikia came after a meeting attended by head coach Gautam Gambhir, ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, BCCI president Mithun Manhas and Saikia.The secretary had already backed Rohit before the Lord's match, saying on July 17: “Rohit is a regular member of the Indian ODI team, and he will continue to represent the country as long as he is in the scheme of things. In other words, the Lord's ODI won't be his last match.”Rohit's age remains an unavoidable part of the discussion. He will turn 40 in 2027, the year of the next ODI World Cup, and India will inevitably have to consider succession planning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Clean Bowled! Yuzvendra Chahal’s magical delivery leaves Ben Stokes stunned in County Championship — Watch
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Yuzvendra Chahal produced a moment of magic in the County Championship on Thursday, leaving Ben Stokes completely baffled with a stunning d.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Yuzvendra Chahal produced a moment of magic in the County Championship on Thursday, leaving Ben Stokes completely baffled with a stunning delivery that crashed into the England all-rounder’s stumps.Playing for Northamptonshire against Durham in Division Two, Chahal bowled Stokes for 14 on the second day at the County Ground in Northampton. The dismissal came in the 47th over with Durham struggling at 187 for six, and the manner in which the veteran leg-spinner outfoxed Stokes quickly became one of the talking points of the match.Chahal castles Stokes with a beautyChahal came around the wicket and tossed one up outside off stump. Stokes appeared to have judged the line correctly and opted to defend, but the delivery had other ideas.The ball pitched outside off before turning sharply into the left-hander. Stokes' bat came down without covering the gap between bat and pad, allowing the ball to sneak through and smash into the top of off stump.Stokes could only stand and stare at the pitch in disbelief before walking back to the pavilion, while Chahal celebrated with his Northamptonshire teammates.The wicket was Chahal's third of the innings and capped a superb spell for the Indian spinner. He finished with figures of 4/36 from 15.2 overs as Durham were bowled out for 205 in 56.2 overs.David Bedingham top-scored for Durham with 81 off 91 balls, while Mayank Agarwal contributed 36. Alex Lees made 24 before becoming another of Chahal's victims.Stokes has had trouble against Indian spinnersThe dismissal was another reminder of Stokes' recent struggles against Indian spin in County cricket.In a previous County Championship outing against Gloucestershire, Stokes appeared well set before Sai Kishore produced a delivery that ended his innings at 45. The Durham all-rounder had struck seven fours and a six in a quick 43-ball knock before being outfoxed.Chahal's latest dismissal was even more spectacular, with the ball turning sharply enough to beat both Stokes' judgement and defence.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Why Ajit Agarkar was not present in BCCI's meeting? Devajit Saikia reveals the reason
articles.summary: Cricket News: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia on Thursday cleared the air over chief selector Ajit Agarkar’s absence from the board’s review meeting, while dismissing.
articles.body: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia on Thursday cleared the air over chief selector Ajit Agarkar’s absence from the board’s review meeting, while dismissing speculation about changes to the senior men’s selection committee.Agarkar was not present at the meeting, which focused on India’s recent performances and the team’s preparations for a packed international calendar leading up to the 2027 ODI World Cup.Saikia explained that Agarkar was out of station when the meeting was called at short notice and was unable to join virtually because he was in an area with poor connectivity.“Today he (Agarkar) was out of station, so he could not be a part of the meeting. Because this meeting was called at very short notice and our head of the selection committee, Ajit Agarkar, was not in town, he could not join it, and he was in such an area that he could not join online also, despite our best efforts,” Saikia told to reporters after the meeting.No discussion on Agarkar’s future or New Director Of CricketSaikia also rejected reports suggesting that Agarkar’s tenure could be coming to an end or that the BCCI was considering changes to the senior men’s selection committee.“There was no such discussion on this in today's meeting. I do not comment on new rumours. We did not have any such discussions, nor did we have such intentions,” he said.The BCCI secretary also ruled out any discussion about appointing a director of cricket for the men’s team. According to Saikia, the meeting was primarily focused on reviewing India’s performances on recent tours and mapping out preparations for the next phase of the international calendar.“There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was on performances in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka and what we are going to do in the upcoming series before the ODI World Cup, which is our ultimate goal,” he said.The meeting, Saikia clarified, was not about deciding individual player selections or fixing format-wise combinations.“We have not discussed all these things regarding the team selection, team combination, who will be playing in what format. For that, selectors will take a call. Today, the selectors were not part of the discussion. So when the selectors meet to select the team for the West Indies series, as well as thereafter for the New Zealand series, they will consider whatever parameters are to be considered by them,” concluded Saikia.India’s road to 2027 World Cup begins in earnestIndia face a packed schedule over the next several months, with the team set to play Afghanistan in a three-match T20I series before the Asian Games in Japan later this month. The West Indies will then tour India for three ODIs and five T20Is, followed by a demanding multi-format tour of New Zealand featuring two Tests, five ODIs and five T20Is.India will subsequently host Sri Lanka for three ODIs and three T20Is before facing Zimbabwe in a three-match ODI series in January 2027. The marquee assignment will be the five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy against Australia, scheduled to run from January to March 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BCCI meeting decoded: Devajit Saikia reveals big plans for injuries, SENA tours and 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has drawn up a roadmap to address India's recent overseas setbacks, mounting player injuri.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has drawn up a roadmap to address India's recent overseas setbacks, mounting player injuries and preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with secretary Devajit Saikia revealing details of Thursday's high-level review meeting in Mumbai.The meeting, attended by head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer and Centre of Excellence director VVS Laxman, reviewed India's recent tours of Ireland and England as well as the team's preparations for the next phase of the international calendar.Chief selector Ajit Agarkar was absent, but Saikia said there was no controversy behind his non-participation and insisted no discussion took place about his future.'BCCI is working like a well oiled engine'Saikia strongly rejected suggestions of a communication gap between the team management and the Centre of Excellence, particularly after several high-profile injury setbacks.“Everybody is on the same page. BCCI is working in a very well like a well oiled engine," Saikia told reporters."There is proper coordination amongst all the wings of BCCI, whether it is women's teams committees or their technical staff or their coaches, vis-a-vis the COE, vis-a-vis the Indian men's team’s coaching staff and the head coach. There is no difficulty in the coordination, everything is moving in the right direction.”However, he admitted that the frequency of injuries remains a major concern and said the board intends to address it through changes to the next Future Tours Programme (FTP).“The only challenge which we are facing is that there are too many matches in the year and that is why in the next FTP we will do certain things, we will take certain measures.”The proposed changes will particularly affect preparation for tours to SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.“We have instructed our FTP persons who will be meeting very soon in various international forums that our FTP should be in such a way it should be scheduled that there is proper rest for the players as well as some kind of acclimatisation or some kind of friendly matches before any major series in SENA countries,” Saikia said.The comments come after India suffered a difficult run in overseas white-ball cricket, losing 0-2 to Ireland in the T20Is before a 1-4 defeat to England in the five-match series. India also lost the ODI series in England 1-2.'We have to do certain soul searching'Saikia acknowledged India's shortcomings and said the review meeting focused on understanding why the team had struggled.“We discussed (about) our team performed in England and Ireland and also about what we are going to do about the next one year. The road map has been prepared and we will be doing some exercises so that we have a very good performance in 2027 (ODI) World Cup,” he said.“Yes, we did not do well. We lost matches in Ireland and England, so we wanted to know what the reasons were. We have to do certain soul searching about that, and in future, what we will be doing before going to any of the SENA countries, we have chalked out some strategy on that.”The board also revisited its Return to Play protocols, with feedback sought directly from Gill, Iyer and Gambhir.“Today's discussion was totally general in nature, what policy and protocols we have to maintain regarding maintaining the fitness level of every player -- not any individual -- and what is best interest of the team, we have considered that only,” Saikia said.“We have taken the feedback from the captains and the head coach who are the right persons to give us the information, so that we chalk up a proper strategy to avoid all this kind of unwanted situations during matches.”Rohit speculation addressed, Agarkar absence explainedSaikia also pushed back against renewed speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma's ODI future and his prospects of playing at the 2027 World Cup.“He is playing superbly in all the matches. So, what more do you want? In the last match, he scored 138 runs. So, why there is a speculation? So, I don't want to give fodder to the speculations,” Saikia said.Rohit had scored a century at Lord's in his last ODI appearance, intensifying the debate over whether he would continue until the 2027 World Cup.Saikia also explained why Agarkar was absent from the meeting.“Today he (Agarkar) was out of station, so he could not be a part of the meeting. Because this meeting was called at very short notice and our head of the selection committee, Ajit Agarkar, was not in town, he could not join it, and he was in such an area that he could not join online also, despite our best efforts,” he said.“There was no such discussion on this in today's meeting. I do not comment on new rumours. We did not have any such discussions, nor did we have such intentions.”He further ruled out any discussion about appointing a new director of cricket.“There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was on performances in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka and what we are going to do in the upcoming series before the ODI World Cup, which is our ultimate goal,” Saikia said.BCCI still searching for sports science chiefThe vacant Head of Sports Science and Medicine position at the CoE was another issue addressed by Saikia, who insisted it had not affected the centre's functioning.“I would like to reiterate once more that the vacant position of the head of the sports science is not a deterrent of our activities in COE,” he said.“(Filling) that post is required, but that is a very high level post, and for that, a proper qualified person should be positioned. We have about 16 persons in place to maintain the fitness level or the rehab facilities.”“To supervise that one important person is required, and for that he must be qualified up to a different level. That kind of person is very less in number in India, as well as in the whole world.“We are trying to find out that kind of a person at the earliest possible time but without him also it is running in the right manner,” Saikia added.The meeting, therefore, ended without any major immediate personnel changes, but with the BCCI setting out a broader plan: reduce the burden of an overcrowded calendar, improve overseas preparation, strengthen injury management and build towards the 2027 World Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI breaks silence on Asian Games concerns, Saikia promises ‘best facilities’ for India cricketers
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has moved to allay concerns over accommodation and logistical arrangements for the Indian .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has moved to allay concerns over accommodation and logistical arrangements for the Indian cricket squads at the upcoming Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, with secretary Devajit Saikia insisting there is no immediate issue but promising that the board will step in if required.Questions had emerged over the facilities available for participating cricket teams ahead of the multi-sport event in Japan, particularly around accommodation and infrastructure. The Japan Cricket Association (JCA) has said teams have been offered hotel accommodation and are also free to make their own arrangements.Speaking after Thursday's review meeting at BCCI headquarters in Mumbai, Saikia said the board was confident about India's arrangements and would not hesitate to create its own system if the situation demanded it.“There is no such issue that we have discussed or which is on our agenda today or prior to today also. So we are not going to have any difficulties in Japan. If any kind of situation arises, we will take an appropriate call at the right time so that we ensure that our players and the support staff will get the best facilities in the Asian Games, whether it is from the organisers.“If required, BCCI will have its own system in place to provide the best facilities to our players,” Saikia told reporters.Japan accommodation concernsThe reassurance comes amid wider logistical questions surrounding the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Organisers confirmed last week that accommodation had been secured for all registered athletes and officials despite entries exceeding 17,000, with participants set to be housed across hotels, temporary accommodation and a cruise ship rather than a traditional athletes' village.For cricket, JCA chief executive officer Naoki Alex Miyaji had sought to ease concerns by saying participating teams were being offered hotel accommodation.India will enter the Asian Games as defending champions in both men's and women's T20 cricket. The men's side will be led by Shreyas Iyer, while Harmanpreet Kaur will captain the women's side.Laxman to lead men's sideVVS Laxman, director of cricket at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, will take charge of the men's side in Japan. He will be assisted by Sunil Joshi, Hrishikesh Kanitkar and Subhadeep Ghosh.Laxman was also in charge when India won the men's gold medal at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.Regular head coach Gautam Gambhir will remain with the senior side for the home ODI series against the West Indies, beginning September 27.The women's side will be coached by Amol Muzumdar, with Aavishkar Salvi and Munish Bali assisting him.India's men's campaign will begin on September 24, while the women's side will enter at the quarterfinal stage, where it is scheduled to face Japan.With both squads packed with established international names and promising youngsters, the BCCI's priority will now be to ensure that logistical concerns do not affect India's bid to retain both Asian Games cricket titles.Indian Squads at Asian Games 2026:Indian men's team: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Shivam Dube, Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Indian women's team: Harmanpreet Kaur (captain), Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh, Gunalan Kamalini, Bharti Fulmali, Sree Charani, Renuka Thakur, Kranti Gaud, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav, Nandani Sharma.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan cricket: Nasser Hussain says dramatic changes from board in England series have made side a 'laughing stock'
articles.summary: Pakistan director of high performance Aaqib Javed says an inquiry will take place after opening batter Imam-ul-Haq, who has now been dropped, does not bat in either innings of second Test at Lord's; Imam among seven players axed ahead of Edgbaston; head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed also removed
articles.body:
Pakistan, 2-0 down after heavy defeats at Headingley and Lord's, have axed seven players for the finale at Edgbaston from September 9, including opener Imam-ul-Haq, wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, spinner Ali Usman and seamer Khurram Shahzad.

Of the seven replacements, only two have played at Test level before in batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal.

Pakistan also removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson in charge for the remainder of the tour.

Hussain, who spoke in frustration during Pakistan's 194-run loss at Lord's about how the tourists had faded as a force, said on the latest Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, as he and Michael Atherton were joined by Cricinfo senior editor Osman Samiuddin: "It is classic 'how you don't build a team' and fans deserve a little bit better.

"With the great teams, it's all about the greater purpose - whether that's Sir Viv Richards and Sir Clive Lloyd with West Indies bringing the islands together or the great Australia side playing for the baggy green cap under Steve Waugh.

"You create a side by making players feel wanted, so the ignominy of sending senior players home - okay, Rizwan has played a couple of bad shots, but he would give his heart and soul for Pakistan cricket.

"However well they go at Edgbaston, the players and coaches will know that the first time they fail that this may well happen to them.

"The point of an administration is to alleviate pressure, not put more pressure on. I cannot see how an administration cannot see that. This may be a stroke of genius but it hasn't worked in the past, so why should it work now?"

How can a director of high performance 'throw a player under the bus'?

Aaqib Javed, the Pakistan Cricket Board's director of high performance, told a TV station in his homeland that drastic action had to be taken as "the world is laughing at us because we can't even compete".

Javed also launched an astonishing attack on Imam, saying the 30-year-old would face an inquiry after not batting in either innings at Lord's due to a calf issue.

He said to Geo : "The Imam injury is a big question mark, and a deep disappointment. Players in the past used to get injuries but used to put on casts and still tried [to play].

"We'll take action against this. How is it possible that a pulled muscle ruled you out of batting in both innings? He should have tried and fought. He'll have to face an inquiry. I can't say he faked it, but a muscle pull like that cannot stop you batting altogether."

Hussain said: "I don't think after Headingley that the world was laughing at Pakistan.

"My rant at Lord's about them not fighting back, about India vs Pakistan games being very one-sided and that they were a poor side playing poorly wasn't laughing at them.

"It was out of frustration of seeing where this great cricketing nation is now. What they have done now is make them into a laughing stock. They have made it worse."

On the Imam situation, Hussain added: "I cannot believe how a director of high performance can go on telly, rightly or wrongly, and throw a player under the bus. He is either injured or he is not.

"For every other touring side, if we ask how a player is doing, they would say, 'he has had a scan and will only bat if needed'. The whole handling of the Iman situation is ridiculous. You have to protect your players a little bit."

Atherton feels for Pakistan captain Babar

Asked by Hussain whether a win for Pakistan in Birmingham would justify such radical moves, Atherton said: "Not in this instance, no, because of the damage it will do longer term.

"This is no way to manage players and no way to build a long-term vision at all.

"I feel it's a horrible position for a captain, Babar Azam, to be in - and what kind of authority does he or indeed any captain of Pakistan have in this outfit?

"One understands that captain is not all powerful these days, you're not going back 30 years ago when they perhaps ran the show, but they have to have some authority within a team.

"Given what's happened, how do you lead that team now?"

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana equals Mithali Raj’s big record, then creates more history
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana added another major milestone to her already glittering international career on Thursday, equalling Mithali Raj's record fo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana added another major milestone to her already glittering international career on Thursday, equalling Mithali Raj's record for the most 50-plus scores in women's international cricket during India's Women's Asia Cup clash against Hong Kong China in Dubai.Mandhana brought up her half-century off 40 balls, reaching the landmark in style by smashing Iqra Sahar over deep backward square-leg for a six. It was her 93rd 50-plus score in women's international cricket, taking her level with India's legendary former captain Mithali Raj at the top of the list.The milestone came during an innings in which Mandhana went on to produce one of the most extraordinary T20I performances of her career.Mithali, who retired from international cricket in 2022, had held the record outright with 93 scores of 50 or more across formats. Mandhana's latest half-century finally brought her alongside the Indian batting great.England's Charlotte Edwards is third on the list with 80 50-plus scores, followed by New Zealand's Suzie Bates on 79 and West Indies great Stafanie Taylor and South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt on 74 each.Most 50-plus scores in women’s international cricket93 - Mithali Raj93 - Smriti Mandhana80 - Charlotte Edwards79 - Suzie Bates74 -Stafanie Taylor74 - Laura WolvaardtMandhana matches Mithali, then shifts gearsHaving equalled Mithali's landmark, Mandhana transformed her innings from controlled aggression into an astonishing assault.The left-hander took just 17 deliveries to move from 50 to 100, completing her second T20I century in only 57 balls.In the process, Mandhana became the first Indian woman to score two T20I centuries. Her first had come against England at Trent Bridge in 2025, when she made 112.Her latest hundred also took her tally to 18 centuries in women's international cricket, moving her ahead of Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt, who have 17 each.Mandhana eventually departed in the final over after smashing 124 off 64 balls, with her spectacular innings containing 14 fours and seven sixes.The knock also became the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119 against Malaysia in 2024.Another record partnership with ShafaliMandhana's latest landmark also came alongside another record involving her long-time opening partner Shafali Verma.The pair's 50-plus partnership was their 29th in T20Is, comfortably the most by any pair in the format. UAE's Esha Oza and Theertha Satish are second on the list with 23, while Australia's Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney have 20.Across formats, Mandhana and Shafali have now registered 44 50-plus partnerships in women's internationals. The next-best pair is New Zealand's Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates, with 37.Mandhana also strengthened her position at the top of the list for 50-plus scores in women's T20Is, with her latest effort taking her tally to 37. Australia's Beth Mooney is next with 33.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BCCI’s big plan for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: ‘Serve like Sachin Tendulkar, not be a one-year wonder’
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is taking a long-term view of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's astonishing rise, with secretary Deva.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is taking a long-term view of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's astonishing rise, with secretary Devajit Saikia revealing that the board is closely monitoring the 15-year-old and wants to ensure his early success translates into a long and distinguished international career.Sooryavanshi's rapid emergence was among the matters discussed at Thursday's high-level BCCI review meeting in Mumbai, which was attended by Saikia, India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, Centre of Excellence (CoE) head VVS Laxman and other senior officials.The teenager has already gone from being an IPL sensation to becoming India's youngest men's international debutant, and the BCCI is now determined to ensure that his development is handled carefully rather than allowing the weight of expectation to derail his progress.“We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or any player of his stature to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends,” Saikia said.“So we look at Vaibhav in a very serious manner. He's monitored from every angle and every step he is taking forward in his international career. The BCCI is taking a very close look at his future.”‘We don’t want a one-series or one-year wonder’Saikia made it clear that the BCCI's objective is not simply to maximise Sooryavanshi's immediate impact but to build a career that can last for years.“You see, the BCCI can be proud that we are promoting a player of the age of 15 years who is already making his mark in the international scenario and we are very cautious that every right step he should take forward so that it should not be a one series or one year wonder,” he said.The comparison with Tendulkar was particularly significant. Like Sooryavanshi, Tendulkar was thrust into the international spotlight as a teenager before going on to enjoy one of the longest and most successful careers in the history of the game.The BCCI secretary stressed that Sooryavanshi's progress would be closely tracked at every stage.“We want Vaibhav's relevance, or any player of his stature, to continue and serve as Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends,” Saikia said.The teenager's rapid rise has given the board plenty of reason for optimism. He was India's youngest-ever men's international debutant after earning his maiden call-up following a sensational IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals.Sooryavanshi scored 776 runs in 16 matches at a strike rate of 237.30, including a century and five fifties, while his 72 sixes set an IPL record for a single season. He subsequently won several awards, including the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker and Super Sixes honours.He also made an immediate impact for India against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches as India completed a 3-0 sweep and claimed his maiden Player of the Series award.His development has continued in domestic cricket. At 15 years and 157 days, he recently became the youngest batter to score a half-century in Duleep Trophy history, breaking a record that had stood for 57 years.Sooryavanshi part of bigger BCCI talent poolImportantly, the BCCI's focus is not limited to Sooryavanshi. Saikia revealed that the board has identified a larger group of emerging players who are being monitored through the CoE.“That our selectors are looking, we have a huge number of upcoming players who are doing good. If you look at our U19 Indian team, they are becoming champions recently also. Similarly, in women's cricket also, we are world champions for the last two international U19 T20 World Cups,” he said.“So we are looking at all the players, not only Vaibhav's relevance, but there are about 10-15 players who are in our targeted group. Those are named in our targeted group list, and they are constantly monitored by our COE head, VVS Laxman, who is taking keen interest in their future and their training and skill development.”Laxman's direct involvement gives Sooryavanshi and the other youngsters access to the BCCI's central development structure as they make the difficult transition from age-group cricket to senior international cricket.The approach also reflects the board's desire to avoid rushing talented youngsters simply because of their early success.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Ireland 165 (47 overs): Hunter 64 (96); Wong 5-33

England 166-4 (23 overs): Bouchier 45 (31); McCartney 2-45

England won by six wickets; lead series 2-0

England sealed a comfortable series win as they hammered Ireland by six wickets in a one-sided encounter in the second one-day international at Derby.

Fast bowler Issy Wong took 5-33 - her first international five-wicket haul - as Ireland were dissmissed for 165 before England cruised to their target in 23 overs to take the series with a match to spare.

Though England made light work of the chase, they were guilty of throwing away their wickets.

Openers Maia Bouchier and Sophia Dunkley, who starred in England's record-breaking chase in the opener at Leicester, started positively with a stand of 54 in seven overs.

Bouchier, who made 45 off 31 balls, inexplicably ran Dunkley out for 20 before also carelessly being caught off a short ball from spinner Kia McCartney.

Alice Capsey was pinned lbw for one and Jodi Grewcock chipped one to mid-wicket for 24, but all-rounders Freya Kemp and Dani Gibson safely steered England to victory with an unbroken stand of 41.

Ireland's batters impressed in the opener by posting 281 but their lack of depth was exposed without contributions from the experienced duo of Gaby Lewis or Orla Prendergast here.

After Wong bowled Lewis for 19, Amy Hunter held firm with her second fifty in as many games, but struggled for support from elsewhere as she fell to Wong for 64 and Ireland lost their last six wickets for 25 runs.

The series and England's international summer concludes at Worcester on Sunday.

Though England won the opener comfortably, their bowlers were unthreatening on a flat pitch in Leicester and struggled to take consistent wickets without Lauren Bell and Sophie Ecclestone, who are resting for the series.

But Wong continued her resurgence under Charlotte Edwards' reign, and appeared to thrive with the responsibility of leading the attack as Lauren Filer was rested.

She bowled Ireland captain Lewis with a nip-backer before Prendergast wasted her solid start before holing out to deep mid-wicket for 25 off Mady Villiers.

Villiers also removed Rebecca Stokell for three, exposing Ireland's fragile middle to lower order for Wong to clean up, and they could not cope with her pace and accuracy.

Ireland managed just 10 boundaries in their innings and, to highlight the mismatch in the teams, Bouchier struck nine alone in her knock.

As the wickets tumbled, the pressure was on Hunter to steer Ireland to a competitive total, but she was caught on the boundary for Wong's fifth wicket to end a gritty 96-ball stay.

The game at Leicester was Wong's first ODI since 2024, and though the batting line-up was not of the highest quality, this was a performance that will please England and Edwards as her transition from bright, emerging talent to potential attack leader develops.

articles.title: County Championship: Sussex's Henry Crocombe takes another hat-trick
articles.summary: Sussex paceman Henry Crocombe takes a second hat-trick in consecutive games as Essex lose their last seven wickets for six runs.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Ambassador Cruise Line Ground, Chelmsford (day two)

Sussex 275: Leaning 60; Porter 4-44 & 90-4: Coles 29*; Harmer 2-19

Sussex (4 pts) lead Essex (3 pts) by 188 runs

Henry Crocombe claimed his second hat-trick in eight days, and third five-wicket haul of the season, to leave Essex's batting in total disarray on an incredible evening of tumbling wickets at Chelmsford.

The 24-year-old seamer, who leaves Sussex for Surrey at the end of the season, had never taken three wickets in successive balls before running through Somerset's tail at Hove last week.

For an encore he helped reduce Essex from 171-3 to 177 all out in the space of 26 balls, his five wickets coming in 14 deliveries without conceding a run. He finished with 5-39.

Essex had been progressing serenely after tea on the second day of the County Championship match when Charlie Allison became Crocombe's first victim after a tidy 56.

That wicket exposed the tender underbelly of Essex's batting and revived fears of a battle against relegation in the run-in to the Division One season.

The collapse gave Sussex an unexpected first-innings lead of 98 after they had taken their score to 275 in the morning, thanks largely to the re-engaged Ari Karvelas thrashing six fours in a breezy 38 from 44 balls.

However, they lost Tom Haines, Tom Clark, Charlie Tear and Oli Carter second time round in extending their advantage to 188 as 11 wickets fell after tea.

Karvelas was not finished when he was last man out in Sussex's first innings and, taking the new-ball, separated the Essex opening pair with an angled a delivery into Paul Walter's stumps. Tom Westley then had a rush of blood and, in attempting to heave Jack Carson over midwicket, was also bowled.

With the sun breaking through and a drying wind, the wicket flattened out and batting seemed to be becoming easier than on day one.

At that stage there was no hint of what was to come. Indeed, Essex reached three figures for two wickets down in 32 overs, 12 quicker than Sussex, the milestone reached with a reverse sweep for four by Allison off Carson.

Allison contributed 38 of a 58-run stand with Dean Elgar before James Coles found extravagant turn with his third ball to bowl Elgar.

Allison's eighth boundary, a drive off Tom Haines, took him to fifty from 60 balls, but he became bogged down, adding only six more from a further 26 balls before he was lbw playing around one from Crocombe.

Then came the carnage. Almost immediately Michael Pepper attempted to sweep Coles and went lbw. Then Crocombe took centre stage. Simon Harmer and Zaman Akhter were both trapped lbw to the first two balls of Crocombe's ninth over before Shane Snater played over the third and lost his leg stump.

Mitch Killeen had been recalled from a loan spell with Gloucestershire to replace Sam Cook, who was called up by England mid-match. Killeen lasted seven balls before he stepped back to try and cut Coles and was bowled. And it wasn't long before Jamie Porter became the sixth player to lose his stumps in the innings, wicket number five for a rampant Crocombe.

Essex took an hour to wrap up the last three Sussex wickets despite Cook removing Dom Goodman playing down the wrong line to the first ball of the morning. That only brought in Karvelas to help Sussex add 62 runs and claim a batting point.

Karvelas was playing a first-class game for the first time in a year after being released by the club. The South African seamer has since worked as a coach in the Sussex academy and been re-signed on a short-term contract to cover injuries and England call-ups.

Jack Leaning put on 36 for the ninth wicket with Karvelas before falling to another catch behind off Akhter for a 110-ball 60. Karvelas was finally out when he edged Porter to give Pepper a fifth catch in the innings and Porter his 600th first-class wicket in figures of 4-44.

articles.title: County Championship: 23 wickets fall on day two between Surrey and Yorkshire
articles.summary: An incredible 23 wickets fall on day two between Surrey and Yorkshire at The Oval, with Surrey chasing 185 to win.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Kia Oval (day two)

Yorkshire 185: Wharton 45; Lawes 4-36 & 82: Luxton 29; Fisher 6-25

Surrey 83: Pope 21; White 3-14 & 27-0: Sibley 15*

Surrey (3 pts) need 158 more runs to beat Yorkshire (3 pts)

Matt Fisher sent England's selectors a clear reminder of his skills by taking a career-best 6-25 against his former county to turn a quite remarkable County Championship match against Yorkshire on its head at the Kia Oval.

Two days after being dropped from England's third Test squad, Fisher was the spearhead as Yorkshire were tumbled out for 82 in their second innings after themselves dismissing Surrey for 83 in 30 overs, as 23 wickets fell on a tumultuous second day.

When the dust settled on the chaos, bad light forcing the players off at 18:20 BST with 15.2 scheduled overs left unbowled, Surrey were 27-0 as they chased 185 for victory.

It is the first time since 1950 that at least a part of all four innings have come on the same day in a first-class game at The Oval, and the first time Surrey and Yorkshire have been bowled out for under 100 by each other since 1967 and 1973, respectively. Only twice before have 23 wickets fallen in a Championship day at The Oval.

In what promises to be a thrilling final month right across Division One, Surrey and Yorkshire – currently eighth and seventh in the table – are both desperate to win this astonishing contest as they try to stay above the two relegation places below them.

The swinging ball has caused havoc so far, with Surrey proving unable to combat Yorkshire's four seamers after Tom Lawes (4-36) had helped to finish off Yorkshire's first innings for 185 in the morning session.

Dom Bess, the number eight, batted as well as anyone for 44 not out off 88 balls but then no one else in either the Surrey or Yorkshire line-ups scored more than Will Luxton's 29 as 20 wickets fell in fewer than 59 overs in the second and third innings of the game.

Ollie Pope's 21 for Surrey, indeed, was the only other individual score above 20, although Bess (17) was one of just three other players to reach double figures.

Fisher's magnificent outswing bowling was backed up well by Lawes, Dan Worrall and Auqib Nabi, while for Yorkshire it was Jack White (3-14), Ben Coad (3-22), George Hill (2-17) and Matt Revis (2-19) who hunted as a highly-disciplined group.

Yorkshire were 133-7 when play began, following the loss of 36 overs to rain and bad light on day one, and for a brief while the bat held sway with Bess and Kuldeep Yadav taking their eighth wicket stand to 57 in the opening 40 minutes.

Those runs seemed more than useful at the time but soon they were approaching gold-dust proportions. Kuldeep's 17 ended when he edged Nabi to second slip and Coad – after a couple of meaty blows – edged Lawes behind on 12. Later in the same over last man White mishit back to bowler Lawes, who dived forward to hold a good low catch.

Surrey's first innings was in trouble early on and they never recovered from losing Rory Burns in the sixth over, Dom Sibley in the eighth and Josh Blake in the ninth.

Burns and Sibley were removed by White, the former under-edging an attempted cut to a ball too full for the shot and the latter edging a leg-cutter to third slip. Left-hander Blake, on two, was leg-before to Coad.

Surrey were 24-3 at lunch and things did not improve afterwards, Ben Foakes (9) edging Hill's medium pace to first slip and Hill then nipping one back at Adam Thomas to have him leg-before for a duck.

From 44-5 much depended on Pope but he drove too early at an away-swinging slower ball from Revis and spooned tamely to mid off.

Lawes went for one, brilliantly held above his head at third slip by Bess from a flashing thick edge off Revis, and Nabi lifted a simple catch to mid off from a leading edge off Coad.

Fisher offered two defiant blows against Revis, a six over backward point and a square cut to the cover ropes, before nicking Coad to first slip. And Rahul Chahar also swung a legside six off Coad but then picked out deep mid wicket trying to repeat the shot against White.

Yorkshire, in the seven overs still to be bowled before tea, lost Adam Lyth and Sam Whiteman for ducks to successive balls from Fisher in the fourth over.

Then came a steady post-tea decline from 36-2, Luxton lifting a drive to mid off, James Wharton bowled by a Nabi beauty and Fisher hitting Jonny Bairstow's off stump through a leaden-footed forward push.

Revis was held at second slip and Hill at second slip, both off Fisher, who then had Kuldeep leg-before for one.

Lawes had Bess caught behind and the innings ended when Coad drove Worrall high to deep cover as Yorkshire were bowled out in 28.5 overs.

articles.title: England seal ODI series win over Ireland after Issy Wong's five-fer in six-wicket victory in Derby
articles.summary: England canter to ODI series-clinching six-wicket victory over Ireland in Derby; Issy Wong (5-33) stars with the ball before England chase down 166 with 27 overs to spare; watch the third and final ODI in Worcester on Sunday (1pm start)
articles.body:
Wong (5-33) recorded career-best figures for England as her five-wicket haul helped bowl Ireland out for 165 in 47 overs after the hosts inserted the tourists at the toss.

Maia Bouchier (45 off 31) top-scored for England as they cruised to their victory target of 166 with 27 overs to spare, Dani Gibson (36no off 22) sealing the emphatic victory with a six.

England's victory secured an unassailable 2-0 series lead before the the teams travel to Worcester for Sunday's third and final ODI, live on Sky Sports.

England clinch ODI series with game to spare

England inserted Ireland after winning the toss and struck after just 10 balls, with the razor-sharp Sophia Dunkley producing a direct hit to run out Alice Tector for three as she sauntered through for a single.

Wong claimed her first wicket in the 10th over, bowling captain Gaby Lewis as Ireland slipped to 33-2 at the end of the powerplay.

Mady Villiers had a hand in England's next two wickets, catching Orla Prendergast on the boundary off Freya Kemp before bowling the delivery that saw Rebecca Stokell hole out to Gibson at cover.

Amy Hunter led the Irish resistance with a gutsy 64 off 96 balls, sharing a 47-run partnership with Prendergast before adding 57 with Leah Paul for the fifth wicket.

But Wong ripped through Ireland's middle order in a devastating spell as Paul, Louise Little and Cara Murray all fell within 19 balls.

Tilly Corteen-Coleman mopped up the Irish tail with the wickets of Jane Maguire and Kia McCartney at the start and end of the 47th over as Ireland set England a modest target of 166 for victory.

A 65-run opening stand between Bouchier and Dunkley laid the foundations for England's chase before a calamitous mix-up between the opened saw Dunkley run out on 20 after hitting two fours and a six.

Jodi Grewcock maintained England's momentum at No 3 before Bouchier was caught off McCartney five runs short of her half-century.

England fell to 85-3 when Alice Capsey departed for one after being trapped lbw by McCartney, but they continued to score at will despite the loss.

A 47-run partnership between Freya Kemp and Gibson saw them home from 119-4 after Grewcock was dismissed, as England got the job done with a staggering 162 balls to spare.

"To win the game like that was phenomenal. To be clinical with the ball [than the first ODI] and then chase the score down, it was brilliant."

Ireland 'struggled to build partnerships'

"It is pretty disappointing. It was a trickier pitch to bat on this morning. Amy Hunter did well to stick in but we struggled to build partnerships and put the pressure on.

"England were more accurate and better in the field. We struggled to take that little extra risk - but we did take four wickets.

"Hopefully we can bounce back in the last game. You can't get too down."

"I had a good chat with members of the staff and a really good chat with our media guy Dean, who really helped flip my mindset. So thanks, Dean!

"It is about doing what the team needs from me. At the moment, I feel like that is hitting the stumps as much as possible.

"I am using my wobble seam to help me do that."

"She alluded to me before today's game that she was going to bowl the wobble seam ball to get a bit more consistency.

"She hit the same area every time, kept being simple. But you wouldn't want her to lose that. The wobble ball is her stock ball, but the one that swings away is the one to go.

"Wong's consistency was the most impressive thing today. I think that's what she'll be most pleased about. England are looking for someone who can back up Lauren Bell with the new ball.

"If Wong can continue to be that consistent, they'll be a formidable pair going forward."

articles.summary: Henry Crocombe takes second hat-trick in as many games for Sussex; Yorkshire and Surrey trade blows with the ball in action-packed day two that sees 23 wickets fall; Ben Stokes takes 3-40 but is bowled by wonder delivery from Yuzvendra Chahal
articles.body:
His sensational outing marked his third five-wicket haul in the County Championship this campaign, and just his second professional hat-trick after his first came against Somerset's tail in his side's last County Championship game.

Crocombe - who is set to sign for Surrey at the end of the season - finished the innings with an impressive 5-39, leaving his side with a first-innings lead of 102, which was extended to 188 by the end of play with Sussex 90-4 on day two.

Elsewhere, Surrey and Yorkshire traded blows with the ball in an incredible day two at the Oval that featured a staggering 23 wickets falling.

Jack White (3-14), Ben Coad (3-22), George Hill (2-17) and Matt Revis (2-19) led the charge for a Yorkshire bowling attack that skittled their opponents for 83, with only four players reaching double figures and Ollie Pope topping the Surrey scoring with a meek 21 off 44.

Yorkshire, though were subjected to their own skittling straight afterwards as they were bowled out for 82 having been 36-2, with Matt Fisher (6-25) dominating a batting lineup that featured just three players reaching double figures and notching just 46 runs for the final eight wickets.

Surrey - 27-0 in their second innings at close of play - need 158 to win to claim just their second County Championship win of the season.

Former England captain Ben Stokes was the victim of a wonder delivery by Northamptonshire spinner Yuzvendra Chahal on Thursday but responded with three wickets for Durham .

Chahal produced his best impression of the late Shane Warne's memorable 'Ball of the Century' in the 1993 Ashes when the former India bowler sent down a delivery which pitched outside off stump before it spun back dramatically to dismiss Stokes for 14.

articles.title: England vs Ireland: Issy Wong rewarded for 'keeping things simple' as five-wicket haul helps side secure ODI series win
articles.summary: Issy Wong bags her best England figures of 5-33 as wobble-seam delivery rips through Ireland; fast bowler delighted hard work pays off; Sky Sports' Tash Farrant feels Wong could be Lauren Bell's long-term new-ball partner; watch final England vs Ireland ODI on Sky Sports on Sunday
articles.body:
But the seamer was rewarded for simplicity on Thursday as a five-wicket haul - her first in international cricket - helped her side wrap up an one-day international series win over Ireland.

Prioritising the wobble-seam delivery that angled in to the right handers, Wong bowled opposition captain Gaby Lewis through the gate for her first strike of the day.

Her relentless targeting of the stumps also saw her clean up Leah Paul off an inside edge, while her three other victims, including top-scorer Amy Hunter, were caught.

Wong had struggled for accuracy during England's victory in the series opener at Leicester on Tuesday, conceding four wides in a row as she curled balls too far past off stump.

She was much improved in Derby, and her display enthused Sky Sports Cricket expert Tash Farrant.

"She hit the same area every single time and kept things simple," Farrant said of Wong after England's six-wicket victory followed the same result two days earlier.

"Wong was struggling so much with consistency two or so years ago but the reason she got a five-fer here was the consistency. She pretty much hit that bail-trimming length every delivery.

"Sometimes with Wong, I think she has all the skills and wants to show them all. Here, she just bowled those wobble balls angling in towards the stumps."

Could Wong form 'formidable' new-ball pairing with Bell?

With premier seamer Lauren Bell rested for this series, Wong has played her first ODIs since the tour of Ireland in 2024, taking her to six matches in the format in total.

She first featured in 50-over cricket for her country back in 2022 but has never been able to grab a regular place, with previous run-up issues contributing to that. Now, though, she has a big opportunity.

Farrant added: "England are looking for someone who can back-up Bell with the new ball and if Wong can be that consistent, they could be a formidable pair going forward."

Farrant's fellow Sky Sports pundit Ravi Bopara does not want Wong to completely jettison the out-swinger, saying having that delivery in her armoury can help her "progress her game to the next level", but her method worked a treat against Ireland.

Wong told reporters: "Even in the last three months, I feel like I've come on a lot. It feels like I've worked quite hard and I guess when you work hard good things happen.

[More responsibility] brings the best out of me. Me and Lauren Filer have got to pick the balls whereas Bell usually does that."

Wong had also spoken when collecting her player-of-the-match award about how chats with staff, including media manager Dean Wilson, had helped her "mindset".

Whoever told her to focus on the wobble seam played a blinder.

articles.title: He started playing at three-and-a-half; two decades later, reached the highest-ever T20I rating: How Abhishek Sharma conquered the fastest format
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma has come a long way from the little boy in Amritsar who first picked up a cricket bat at the age of three-and-a-half. On his birthday,.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma has come a long way from the little boy in Amritsar who first picked up a cricket bat at the age of three-and-a-half. On his birthday, his journey stands out as one of the most remarkable rises in modern T20 cricket, from a promising youngster in Punjab to an India regular and the holder of the highest-ever ICC T20I batting rating.The boy who started cricket at three-and-a-halfAbhishek's father, Raj Kumar Sharma, a former cricketer, introduced him to the game when he was just three-and-a-half. The youngster quickly developed an obsession with batting and progressed through Punjab's age-group system.His numbers soon began attracting attention. During the 2015-16 Vijay Merchant Trophy, Abhishek scored more than 1,200 runs at an average of 109.09 and also claimed 57 wickets. He captained Punjab to the Under-19 Asia Cup title in 2016 before becoming part of India's victorious Under-19 World Cup campaign in 2018.The IPL came at just 17, when Delhi Daredevils picked him in the 2018 auction. His career, however, did not explode immediately. Abhishek spent several seasons developing his game through domestic cricket and the IPL before finding the perfect platform for his aggressive style.Yuvraj Singh's influence shapes his fearless approachA major influence during that period was Yuvraj Singh. The former India all-rounder became Abhishek's mentor and worked closely with him, particularly during the Covid-19 lockdown. Yuvraj understood the youngster's attacking instincts and encouraged him to embrace them rather than become overly cautious. That philosophy eventually became the foundation of Abhishek's T20 game.His international breakthrough came after making his T20I debut in July 2024. In February 2025, Abhishek produced one of the most devastating T20I innings by an Indian batter when he smashed 135 off just 54 balls against England in Mumbai. The innings contained 13 sixes and a 37-ball century, announcing him as one of India's most dangerous T20 batters.From breakthrough star to world-record holderThe 135 was only the beginning. During the 2025 Asia Cup, Abhishek established himself as India's attacking force at the top of the order. He scored 314 runs in seven matches at a strike rate of 200 and was named Player of the Tournament as India won the competition.His performances pushed him to the top of the ICC T20I batting rankings and eventually into record-breaking territory. After scoring 61 against Sri Lanka, Abhishek reached 931 rating points, the highest-ever rating achieved by a men's T20I batter.He surpassed Dawid Malan's previous record of 919 and moved beyond the best ratings achieved by India's Suryakumar Yadav and Virat Kohli.A T20 batter built for destructionThe numbers behind Abhishek's rise were extraordinary. In 2025, he became the first player to score more than 1,000 runs in T20 cricket in a calendar year while maintaining a strike rate above 200. He finished the year at a strike rate of 202 and smashed 108 sixes.His IPL performances were equally destructive. Playing for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Abhishek produced a stunning 141 off 55 balls against Punjab Kings in IPL 2025. He reached his fifty in only 16 balls and his century in 40, hitting 14 fours and 10 sixes as Hyderabad chased down 246. The innings broke KL Rahul's record for the highest score by an Indian batter in IPL history.His development has been shaped by several influential figures. Apart from Yuvraj, Abhishek has drawn lessons from players such as Shikhar Dhawan, Brian Lara and Travis Head. At Sunrisers, his partnership with Head showed how effectively his aggressive approach could work against the best bowling attacks.At the 2026 T20 World Cup, Abhishek added another major achievement to his growing list, playing a crucial role in India's title-winning campaign, including a blistering 52 off 21 balls in the final against New Zealand.T20I career so far Abhishek Sharma has played 56 T20Is between 2024 and 2026, scoring 1,629 runs in 55 innings at an average of 30.73 and a remarkable strike rate of 187.24. He has registered two centuries and 11 fifties, with a highest score of 135. His aggressive approach is reflected in his boundary count, with the left-hander hitting 164 fours and 104 sixes in his international career so far.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana has already established herself among the finest batters in women's cricket, but on Thursday she reached a new pinnacle — becoming the most prolific run-scorer in the history of the women's game.During India's Women's Asia Cup 2026 clash against Hong Kong China in Dubai, the Indian vice-captain surpassed legendary former captain Mithali Raj's tally of 10,868 international runs to become the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket across all formats.And she did it in spectacular fashion.Mandhana produced a breathtaking 124 off 64 balls, smashing 14 fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 193.75 as India posted 193/5 after being asked to bat first. Her record-breaking innings not only took her past Mithali but also established a series of new milestones.Mandhana goes past Mithali in styleMandhana entered the match knowing she was closing in on Mithali's long-standing record. Having already overtaken New Zealand great Suzie Bates to move into second place during the Asia Cup opener against Thailand, the 30-year-old needed one more major push to rewrite the all-time record.She delivered far more than that.Mandhana initially had to negotiate a slow Dubai surface and disciplined Hong Kong bowling. Shafali Verma provided the early acceleration, with the opening pair putting on 50 before Verma departed for 28 off 17 balls.Once Mandhana settled in, however, the innings changed gears.She reached her half-century and then launched an extraordinary assault, moving from 50 to 100 in just 17 deliveries. Her century came off 57 balls before she eventually finished with 124 from 64, her second T20I hundred.Her dismissal came on the final over of the innings following a mix-up with Bharti Fulmali, but by then Mandhana had already rewritten the record books.The 124 also became the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119 against Malaysia in 2024.Most runs in Women’s international cricket10880* - Smriti Mandhana10868 - Mithali Raj10740 - Suzie Bates10273 - Charlotte Edwards10007 - Stafanie TaylorFrom Mithali's record to a pile of milestonesMandhana's landmark innings did not stop with the all-time runs record.Her century took her international hundred tally to 18, making her the leading century-maker in women's international cricket, ahead of Australia's Meg Lanning and South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt, who had 17 each.She also became the first Indian woman to score two T20I centuries. Her previous hundred had come against England in 2025, when she made 112.The latest innings also extended Mandhana and Shafali's remarkable partnership record. Their 50-plus stand against Hong Kong was their 29th in T20Is, the most by any pair in the format.ALSO READ: Smriti Mandhana equals Mithali Raj’s big record, then creates more historyFor Mandhana, though, the most significant achievement was undoubtedly moving past Mithali.Mithali's 10,868 runs had stood as the benchmark of women's international batting excellence since her retirement in 2022. Mandhana's explosive rise has now taken her beyond that mark, with New Zealand's Suzie Bates, England's Charlotte Edwards and West Indies great Stafanie Taylor completing the top five on the all-time list.What made Thursday's achievement even more remarkable was the manner in which Mandhana reached it. On a surface that offered little pace, she adapted her game, used the back foot effectively and found ways to manufacture boundaries.“Having said that, I just love batting, and I’m happy that I could contribute,” Mandhana said during the mid-innings break.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking knock as India stormed into the Women's Asia Cup semi-final with a 137-run win over Hong Kong on Thursday. .
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana produced a record-breaking knock as India stormed into the Women's Asia Cup semi-final with a 137-run win over Hong Kong on Thursday. The India opener smashed 124 off 64 balls, helping her side post 193 for five before Hong Kong were bowled out for 56 in 16.2 overs.Mandhana's century was her second in T20 internationals and made her the only Indian woman to achieve the feat. She also moved past Meg Lanning for the most international centuries in women's cricket, reaching 18 hundreds across formats. Later in the innings, she surpassed Mithali Raj to become the leading run-scorer in women's internationals.Despite the historic nature of her innings, Mandhana admitted she was unaware of the records she had broken."I didn't know all of this happened," Mandhana said after being informed about her record-breaking effort.Asked who she would dedicate the century to, the Player of the Match said her family remained closest to her heart."I don't have anyone in mind who I would like to dedicate, but definitely, my family."Mandhana also explained how she approached the Hong Kong attack, having never faced the opposition before."We’re not really aware of (the opposition). We had seen a few videos, but not really aware. We’re playing them for the first time, so when you come against a bowler who you don’t know a lot, you have to just forget that you’ve played whatever cricket. You just have to go, watch the ball, and I think it was more about just adjusting to the pace."The left-hander initially took some time to settle before accelerating alongside Shafali Verma, who scored 28 off 17 balls. Mandhana eventually struck seven sixes and 14 boundaries, making batting look effortless despite the surface not being particularly easy for strokeplay.She was also asked about missing out on some full tosses during the powerplay and admitted that such deliveries are not necessarily her strength."I would say that full tosses are not my strength (laughs). I’m happy that I could get away with a few of the full tosses today. I think any top-order batter would say that sometimes full tosses can go for a six, or you can get out."Mandhana had earlier acknowledged Hong Kong's disciplined bowling, particularly during the powerplay."It's really hard for me to play slower bowlers, but credit to them. They were really disciplined in the powerplay. They bowled pretty well, and the kind of energy they showed was something which we all can learn from. Having said that, I just love batting, and I'm happy that I could contribute."India secured their second win in as many matches and will face Pakistan on Saturday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Engineer by day, cricketer by night: The unlikely journey of Anshuman Hooda
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Anshuman Hooda bursts into laughter when asked to choose between his office laptop and his cricket ball. “My cricket ball is my best friend.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anshuman Hooda bursts into laughter when asked to choose between his office laptop and his cricket ball. “My cricket ball is my best friend,” he tells TimesofIndia.com.His elder brother, Vikram Hooda, says their mother, Prem Lata Singh, a primary class teacher at a Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) school, is happy to see Anshuman pursue cricket, especially now that he has a stable job. “Earlier, they used to say that he needed a job. Now that he has one and is doing well, she is happy,” Vikram says of their parents.Anshuman had a breakout 2026 Delhi Premier League (DPL) season -- emerging as the Purple Cap winner with 22 scalps -- which played a crucial role in South Delhi Superstarz's title triumph.But there was a time when Hooda thought cricket had run its course. Two attempts at the Under-23 trials had gone by without success. There was no age-group cricket on his résumé, no traditional pathway through Delhi's junior system and no obvious route into first-class cricket. He had an engineering degree from Delhi Technological University (DTU) and a job at EY. The sensible thing, he thought, was to move on.“I tried for Under-23 for two years, but I couldn’t make it. I thought it would be very difficult because I hadn’t played any professional cricket or age-group cricket. It would have been very difficult to directly get selected for the Ranji Trophy or first-class cricket,” Anshuman recollects.“So at that time, I thought I should quit cricket and pursue my career in engineering or something.”But just when he thought of walking away from the game, his coach Harish Dagar, who runs a cricket academy named Delhi Cricket Hub in Delhi's Paschim Vihar, and trains youngsters at DTU, stepped up.“It was in 2023. He had just graduated. He had got the job through campus placement and was ready to move on with his life. I pleaded with him to give it one more year. I asked him to come to my academy four days a week for a year, and if nothing would pan out, I would let him pursue his corporate job,” reminisces Dagar.I have seen some substantial progress in my cricket in recent months and in this tournament. So in the coming times, I might shift my whole focus to cricket and give it my all.Then came the Delhi Premier League (DPL). And with it came a completely different possibility. For a young man who had arrived late to leather-ball cricket, DPL became the stage on which his raw pace, athleticism and appetite for fast bowling could finally be seen. The numbers followed. The attention followed, and now Anshuman is finally ready to become a full-time cricketer.“I have seen some substantial progress in my cricket in recent months and in this tournament. So in the coming times, I might shift my whole focus to cricket and give it my all,” he says.The boy who skated before he bowledAnshuman is 25 and, in cricketing terminology, he can be called a late bloomer. But the most unusual thing about Anshuman's story is perhaps where it began. Not with a cricket academy. Not with a junior tournament. Not with a childhood obsession with bowling. With roller skates.Growing up, Anshuman was a national-level roller skater. Cricket existed around him, but it was not initially the sport that defined him. His elder brother Vikram had played cricket, and there was, as Anshuman puts it, a familiar sibling dynamic. His brother took science. He took science. His brother studied engineering. He studied engineering. But when it came to cricket, Anshuman's journey took its own route.It was only when he reached college that the game began to take hold.“I just started playing in college, and that’s when I got into leather-ball cricket professionally, playing for the college team and all. That’s when I fell in love with bowling fast, getting wickets and the aggression that comes with it. I just loved bowling fast.”I worked on his mind 80-85 per cent. I made him mentally strong. I told him never to think that he was tired or burdened. Once I worked on his mindset and the roadmap was clear in front of him, he knew what he had to do.When cricket had to fit around a careerThat love became the starting point of something neither his résumé nor his previous sporting journey could have predicted.Harish Dagar first noticed Anshuman in 2019 while they were at university. What caught his eye was not a polished fast bowler. It was the physical package.Fitness. Arm speed. Natural movement.Anshuman was playing tennis-ball cricket when Dagar asked him to try medium pace. The first attempts were raw and erratic, but there was enough pace and athletic ability for the coach to believe there was something worth developing.“His body alignment was natural. His strength was natural, and his pace was natural. But he didn't have enough strength in his body initially. That's why I told him that if you don't maintain your fitness along with your natural pace, you will face problems," says Dagar.“He was also busy with his job. He couldn't always take proper sessions. He would come at night, then have to go to the gym and take practice sessions. It was very hectic.“I worked on his mind 80-85 per cent. I made him mentally strong. I told him never to think that he was tired or burdened.“Once I worked on his mindset and the roadmap was clear in front of him, he knew what he had to do. At one point he had to focus on fitness, at another he had to do his job, and then he had to come to me for his sessions."Fast bowling is not a very comfortable activity for the body. You accelerate, then your whole body has to absorb the impact before you bowl. It definitely takes a toll on the body.Anshuman graduated from DTU with a degree in Production and Industrial Engineering and joined a multinational company in 2023. He worked from home, which helped him juggle the demands of employment and an increasingly serious cricket career. But balancing the two was never going to be easy.Fast bowling is an unforgiving craft. It demands strength, recovery, repetition and hours of training. Dagar's approach was to build Anshuman patiently, focusing not merely on speed but on the physical and mental foundations that could allow him to bowl fast consistently.Anshuman also had to understand his own body. He had dealt with niggles and the physical toll that comes with repeatedly accelerating, landing and transferring his entire body weight through a bowling action.“Fast bowling is not a very comfortable activity for the body. You accelerate, then your whole body has to absorb the impact before you bowl. It definitely takes a toll on the body,” he says.But there was no great mystery behind his motivation. He adds: “It was just the love for the sport and the love for bowling fast that kept me motivated and helped me come back stronger every time.”That attitude has been central to his development.The making of a fast bowlerDagar describes the next stage of the process in more professional terms: periodisation, rest, strength work, workload scheduling, diet, physiotherapy and technical skills. Anshuman had to develop a stock ball and variations such as the leg-cutter and off-cutter while ensuring that his body could cope with the demands of pace.Shikhar Dhawan himself, the team owner, surprised me. He came and we had a little conversation. He gave me some very good tips and a direction to work towards from here.The objective was never simply to produce a fast delivery. It was to produce a fast bowler. The first real crack in the wall came through the DPL.In 2024, he got his opportunity with South Delhi, initially finding chances hard to come by. Then came a spell that changed perceptions. The next season brought more opportunities, including a five-wicket haul, and soon IPL franchises were looking at him as a net bowler and trial candidate.The journey from someone contemplating quitting cricket to someone attracting franchise attention had happened remarkably quickly. For Anshuman, the attention became tangible when Shikhar Dhawan, the owner of his DPL team, spoke to him after his performances.“Shikhar Dhawan himself, the team owner, surprised me. He came and we had a little conversation. He gave me some very good tips and a direction to work towards from here,” he says.It was a moment of validation. For someone who had spent years outside the conventional cricket pathway, being noticed by an established name carried significance beyond a conversation.Speed is not enoughAt 140 kmph, Anshuman possesses the one commodity that can change a fast bowler's career quickly: pace. Coach Dagar believes there is more to come. Anshuman is not shy about wanting it.“Definitely, speed is what I want. If I can, I will definitely look to bowl even faster and build the strength and skills to do that, while making sure there is no compromise on accuracy and line,” said Anshuman.That final clause is important. Pace can attract attention. Accuracy keeps a fast bowler in a team. For Anshuman, the next challenge is therefore not simply touching a bigger number on the speed gun. It is learning how to sustain high pace across long spells, particularly in red-ball cricket.He is already thinking about it. “These are the things we prepare for. Who bowls in a four-day or five-day game and bowls long spells with the same effort? That is what I am preparing for. If I get an opportunity, I will definitely do that.”Anshuman's ambition is clear. First, Delhi. Then first-class cricket. Then, eventually, IPL and India.“The eventual goal is to play and win matches for the country. That is my ultimate goal,” he says.Job or cricketThere is, however, one more conversation happening in Anshuman's life. The conversation between security and possibility. An engineering degree and a job at a good company offer a predictable future. And he has got a promotion before the start of the DPL season as well. Cricket offers something very different: uncertainty, competition and the possibility of a career that can disappear as quickly as it arrives.Currently, I have joined back. But as I have seen some substantial progress in my cricket in recent months and in this tournament, I might, in the coming times, shift my whole focus to cricket and give it my all.For now, Anshuman has returned to work. But his cricket has progressed to the point where continuing to divide himself between the two may no longer be possible.“Currently, I have joined back. But as I have seen some substantial progress in my cricket in recent months and in this tournament, I might, in the coming times, shift my whole focus to cricket and give it my all.”It is a significant sentence from someone who once thought about quitting the sport altogether. There is also a quiet irony in the fact that the engineer who learned to manage competing demands may soon have to choose one.Anshuman knows where he wants to go.“I will give it my all. Let’s see what happens ahead.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah faces key fitness test before Afghanistan T20Is as Prince Yadav emerges as backup

articles.body: New Delhi: As the Indian team awaits Jasprit Bumrah’s fitness reports ahead of the T20I series against Afghanistan next week and the subsequent Asian Games, the national selectors have identified Prince Yadav as a probable backup.TOI understands that Bumrah, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar and Harshit Rana are due to undergo match simulation tests over the course of this week before the Indian team assembles in Delhi on Sept 10.“The BCCI medical team at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) had shared a report with selectors last week, where it was mentioned that these four players were clinically fit but had to be assessed in practice matches. The CoE has lined up the matches from Sept 4-9. The CoE is confident that the players should be ready for the Afghanistan series,” a BCCI source said.Prince made his international debut in the ODI series against Afghanistan at home in June. He too suffered a hamstring injury in the second T20I in Zimbabwe on July 25.It is learnt that he has been declared fit by the CoE and is available for selection. Prince has been doing well in T20Is since this year’s IPL and the selectors see him as a serious prospect going forward.Selectors want Bumrah to play one FC match before NZ TestsThe selectors and the team management want Bumrah to get some game time in a first-class match before the Test series in New Zealand. Bumrah hasn’t played a red-ball match since the second Test against South Africa in Guwahati last November. He has only played T20 cricket before injuring his knee after two ODIs in England in July.“As it is, he has to skip Test matches because of his fitness. One has to be clear that his knee can take the load of a first-class game before he takes the field in a Test in New Zealand. It needs to be seen if he plays a Ranji Trophy game or a first-class game for India ‘A’ in New Zealand. He is likely to be rested for the T20I series against West Indies at home in October. But the ‘A’ games in New Zealand overlap with the ODI series there,” a source said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
