articles.title: Rohit Sharma remains in contention for 2027 World Cup, BCCI dismisses retirement speculation
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mumbai: Despite speculation over his retirement, Rohit Sharma remains in contention to play next year’s ODI World Cup.The BCCI has reiterated that the.
articles.body: Mumbai: Despite speculation over his retirement, Rohit Sharma remains in contention to play next year’s ODI World Cup.The BCCI has reiterated that there is no imminent threat to the former captain’s place in the side, with his availability and selection for the 2027 World Cup continuing to be a subject of intense discussion.Board secretary Devajit Saikia said he did not want to provide “fodder” for speculation over Rohit’s future and added that the 39-year-old has been playing “superbly”. Questioning the speculation around Rohit, who now plays only ODIs for India, Saikia said: “He is playing superbly in all matches. So what more do you want? In the last match against England, he scored 138 runs, so why is there speculation around his future? I do not want to give any fodder to the speculators.”Saikia was speaking after a performance review of the Indian team at the BCCI headquarters on Thursday.The meeting was attended by India’s captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir and Centre of Excellence head VVS Laxman, along with top BCCI officials. However, chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar was absent. He was out of Mumbai and was reportedly in a no-internet zone.Saikia said there was no discussion on extending Agarkar’s contract.“He was out of station and could not be part of the meeting because it was called at very short notice. So he could not join. He was in such an area that he could not join online either,” Saikia said.Asked whether there was any discussion about extending Agarkar’s tenure as chairman of selectors, Saikia said: “There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was on India’s performance in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka, and what we are going to do in the upcoming series and the World Cup, which is our ultimate goal.”Saikia dismissed speculation about Laxman being appointed BCCI’s director of cricket. India’s performance under Agarkar’s selection panel has been marked by major success in ICC tournaments.Saikia said the BCCI would work on a plan to ensure Indian players get adequate rest, acclimatisation time and practice matches before major series in SENA countries. In the past, India have often arrived in these countries with little match practice, resulting in heavy defeats before adjusting to local conditions.Saikia denied any lack of communication between the national selectors and the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru over injury management, but said the board would look to improve the Future Tours Programme to give players more time to prepare.“Everybody is on the same page. There is proper coordination among all wings of the BCCI. Everything is moving in the right direction,” Saikia said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 65m boundaries, hybrid pitch: Inside the new venue for India’s Asian Games campaign
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai: India’s gold medal defence in cricket at the Asian Games will begin in the quarterfinals on September 28, and there could well be a blockbust.
articles.body: Chennai: India’s gold medal defence in cricket at the Asian Games will begin in the quarterfinals on September 28, and there could well be a blockbuster game against Pakistan a couple of days later.The site of three baseball grounds has been converted into a new facility in Nisshin called Korogi Sports Park, where Japan will get a taste of top-flight cricket.For starters, it’s not as small a ground as the one used during the Hangzhou Asiad four years ago. The shortest boundary at Nisshin is 65 metres, almost 10 metres longer than the facility that hosted cricket at Hangzhou.Adam Birss, technical operations manager for cricket at the Asiad, told TOI that this was possible because the organisers were able to build a ground from scratch, giving them the liberty to use more space, which wasn’t the case in Hangzhou.To help with the preparation of the pitches, the Asian Cricket Council reached out to Sri Lanka Cricket, which sent Asitha Wijayasinghe, the curator of Kandy’s Pallekele International Stadium.Given Pallekele’s high-scoring nature, it will be safe to assume that the facility in Nisshin will see a lot of runs being scored. It can be a welcome relief from what we saw when part of the T20 World Cup in 2024 was held at a makeshift venue at Nassau County ground near New York, with teams struggling to manage 125.In addition to four turf pitches, the ground also has a hybrid pitch consisting of natural clay and synthetic fibres, the technology being used in Australia and Sri Lanka.“The construction allows us to prepare a faster pitch. It is also more forgiving in terms of wear and tear,” Birss said.The clay used for the pitches is local. “The clay content will not only provide bounce for pacers, but also grip for spinners,” Birss added.Drainage a key issueOne of the biggest concerns will be the risk of typhoons, which typically strike Japan around the window in which the Games are scheduled to be held. This makes drainage an important aspect, and Birss informed that adequate measures are being taken.“The ground has been reinforced with a sand base, allowing for more water absorption. However, given that the ground was built with a tight public budget, the drainage cannot be compared with the best around the world,” Birss said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Defending champions Sri Lanka moved to the top of Group B in the Women's Asia Cup after beating Indonesia by 75 runs in Dubai on Thursday, thanks to c.
articles.body: Defending champions Sri Lanka moved to the top of Group B in the Women's Asia Cup after beating Indonesia by 75 runs in Dubai on Thursday, thanks to captain Chamari Athapaththu's record seven-wicket haul and Nilakshika Silva's half-century.Sri Lanka were defending a modest target of 125 on a slow-paced pitch, but Athapaththu turned the match around with one of the best bowling performances in women's T20 internationals.She came on to bowl in the fourth over and struck with her fourth, seventh and eighth deliveries. Although she missed out on a hat-trick in that over, she completed it later by taking three wickets in three balls across two overs.Athapaththu finished with 7/5 in 21 balls, becoming the first bowler from a Full Member nation to take seven wickets in a women's T20I. The previous best figures in women's T20Is belonged to Zimbabwe's Esther Mbofana, who took 6/11 against Eswatini in 2021.Indonesia were bowled out for 49. Rahmawati Pangestuti scored 10, while Ni Made Putri Suwandewi remained unbeaten on 12. No other Indonesian batter reached double figures.Earlier, Sri Lanka were in trouble at 62/6 before Nilakshika Silva scored 50 off 35 balls to lift them to 124/7.For Indonesia, Ni Luh Dewi was the pick of the bowlers with 3/32.The win took Sri Lanka to the top of Group B in the Women's Asia Cup.In Group A, India remain on top of the standings, with Pakistan in second place.Meanwhile, India's vice-captain Smriti Mandhana also made history during India's Group A match against Hong Kong in Dubai. articles.title: ‘Horrible’! Babar Azam’s ‘authority’ questioned after PCB’s dramatic shake-up
articles.summary: Cricket News: Michael Atherton has questioned the authority of Babar Azam and the role Pakistan’s captains are allowed to play after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB.
articles.body: Michael Atherton has questioned the authority of Babar Azam and the role Pakistan’s captains are allowed to play after the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) made sweeping changes to the Test squad midway through the England series.Pakistan suffered defeats in the opening two Tests and responded by sending seven players home. Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha and Imam-ul-Haq were among those removed from the squad, while coaches Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also asked to leave.Mike Hesson will now take charge of the team for the third and final Test at Edgbaston, beginning on September 9.The scale of the changes has placed Babar under increasing scrutiny. Former Pakistan captain Rashid Latif had already argued that Babar should have resigned after the seven players were sent home, while also branding him a “dummy captain”.Atherton has now questioned whether Babar, or indeed any Pakistan captain, has enough influence within the setup to lead effectively following such a major intervention from the board.The former England captain believes the changes could have lasting consequences for Pakistan, regardless of what happens in the final Test.“Not in this instance, no, because of the damage it will do in the long term. This is no way to manage players and no way to build a long-term vision at all,” Atherton said on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.“I feel it's a horrible position for a captain, Babar Azam, to be in - and what kind of authority does he or indeed any captain of Pakistan have in this outfit?” he added.Atherton questions Babar’s authorityAtherton suggested that the events of the England tour could make it extremely difficult for Babar to establish authority over the Pakistan dressing room.He acknowledged that modern-day captains do not have the same control they once enjoyed, but insisted that a captain still needs to have a meaningful say in the team’s affairs.“One understands that the captain is not all-powerful these days, you're not going back 30 years ago when they perhaps ran the show, but they have to have some authority within a team,” said Atherton.The former England captain then raised a question over how Babar can move forward after the PCB’s intervention."Given what's happened, how do you lead that team now?" he added.Babar’s difficult returnBabar reclaimed Pakistan’s Test captaincy from Shan Masood earlier this year after Bangladesh defeated Pakistan in their two-match series.His side subsequently drew the series against the West Indies before travelling to England.The 31-year-old missed the first Test against England because of an injury, but returned for the second match at Lord’s.His comeback, however, did little to ease Pakistan’s batting problems. Babar scored only 8 and 6 as Pakistan suffered another heavy defeat.England won the Lord’s Test by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.With seven players removed and the coaching staff reshuffled, Babar now faces the challenge of leading a significantly altered Pakistan side in the final Test at Edgbaston.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘World laughing at Pakistan?’: Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB slammed for turning team into a ‘laughingstock’
articles.summary: Cricket News: Nasser Hussain has joined the growing criticism of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), accusing the governing body of making the situation worse after t.
articles.body: Nasser Hussain has joined the growing criticism of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), accusing the governing body of making the situation worse after the team suffered defeats in the first two Tests of the three-match series in England.Pakistan were beaten in Headingley and Lord’s, after which the PCB made a sweeping overhaul of the touring set-up. Seven players were sent back from England, while two members of the coaching staff were also removed. The move has attracted criticism from former players and experts across the cricketing world.Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha and Imam-ul-Haq were among those told to return home. Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was also replaced, with Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test in Birmingham, which begins on September 9.The controversy has extended beyond the squad changes. Aaqib Javed, the PCB's director of high performance, criticised Imam on live television and questioned the opener’s commitment to the team.Imam suffered a calf strain on the opening day of the Lord’s Test and was subsequently ruled out of the match. The left-handed batter did not take part with the bat in either innings, while his actions on the fourth day further fuelled questions over the seriousness of the injury.Before play began on the fourth day, Imam was seen knocking the ball around despite his injury. The footage prompted further scrutiny, with former England pacer Stuart Broad famously saying it was all “for show.”Hussain, however, believes the bigger issue lies with how the PCB handled the matter.Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, the former England captain said Pakistan were not initially being mocked following their poor performances, but argued that the PCB's subsequent actions had turned the team into a laughingstock.“I don't think after Headingley that the world was laughing at Pakistan. My rant at Lord's about them not fighting back, about India vs Pakistan games being very one-sided and that they were a poor side playing poorly wasn't laughing at them,” said Hussain.“It was out of frustration of seeing where this great cricketing nation is now. What they have done now is make them a laughingstock. They have made it worse,” he added.Hussain questions Imam handlingHussain then turned his attention to the treatment of Imam, expressing disbelief that a senior official within Pakistan cricket would publicly criticise one of the team's own players.He argued that regardless of whether Imam was genuinely injured or not, the situation should have been handled internally, with the player receiving proper support and respect.“I cannot believe how a director of high performance can go on telly, rightly or wrongly, and throw a player under the bus. He is either injured or he is not,” said Hussain.“For every other touring side, if we ask how a player is doing, they would say, 'he has had a scan and will only bat if needed'. The whole handling of the Iman situation is ridiculous. You have to protect your players a little bit,” he added.The PCB's decisions have now left Pakistan facing the final Test with a significantly altered squad and coaching structure, after a series that had already come under intense scrutiny following two heavy defeats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana: India's opener becomes all-time highest run scorer in women’s international cricket after record century
articles.summary: India opener Smriti Mandhana overtakes Mithali Raj as the record run scorer, across all formats, in women's international cricket; Mandhana also overtakes former Australia captain Meg Lanning for most centuries;
articles.body:
Mandhana smashed 124 runs from 64 deliveries to help India to a 137-run victory over Hong Kong in their second Group A match, as they posted 193-5 from their 20 overs before bowling out their opponents for 56.

The innings saw Mandhana reach 10,880 runs across all three formats for India and pass former captain Mithali Raj to become the all-time leading run-scorer in women's international cricket.

Mandhana's century - containing 14 fours and seven maximums - was her 18th across formats, which also saw her move past former Australia captain Meg Lanning for most centuries in women's international cricket.

"Until I was batting, I didn't know what record [I had broken] because I didn't know what exact runs [I had made]," Mandhana said in the post-match press conference.

"But looking back, I'd say a very good day for Indian cricket. Of course, Mithali [Raj] has been such a legend and a role model. We've all grown up watching her bat, so to go past in the tally of runs is something that I'd definitely not imagined to do."

She added: "Two of the legends of the game: Meg Lanning and Mithali Raj - these are the people I've grown up watching. I've tried to take a lot of things from them as batters, so really happy that I could go past them in whatever ways."

Mandhana made her India debut in 2013 and scored her maiden T20I century last year, becoming the first Indian batter to score a ton across all formats in women's cricket.

Raj, who held the previous record with 10,868 runs across formats, said on X: "Well deserved, @mandhana_smriti . I've watched you grow from a young player into one of the finest batters India has produced.

"To see you go past my record and become the highest run-scorer in international cricket is a moment I'm genuinely proud of. Here's to many more runs and milestones. Keep going!"

The 30-year-old could pass 11,000 runs during the Asia Cup, with India next in action against Pakistan on Saturday.

articles.title: Time to appoint Smriti Mandhana as captain of Indian team in all three formats: Diana Edulji
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: Former India captain Diana Edulji feels it's time to appoint vice-captain and superstar batter Smriti Mandhana as captain of the Indian women'.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Former India captain Diana Edulji feels it's time to appoint vice-captain and superstar batter Smriti Mandhana as captain of the Indian women's team "in all three formats of the game."Mandhana became the leading run-getter in women's internationals, en route to her hundred (124) in the Women's Asia Cup 2026 on Thursday against Hong Kong in Dubai. She broke former Indian women's captain Mithali Raj's record of 10,868 runs. Mandhana also broke the record for most centuries (18) in international cricket, the most by any batter in the women's game, surpassing Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt, who have 17 apiece. Mandhana has two hundreds in T20Is, two in Tests and 14 in ODIs. The elegant left-hander has 93 fifty-plus scores across formats in international cricket, the joint-most by any batter, alongside Raj.It was also Mandhana's second T20I hundred, thus making the 30-year-old the first Indian woman to score multiple centuries in the shortest format of the game.“I congratulate Smriti Mandhana on becoming the leading run-getter in women's internationals. I feel that it's high time that the national women's selection committee, led by Amita Sharma, appoints Smriti as the new captain in all three formats of the game. Harmanpreet Kaur can continue to play as a senior player in the side,” Edulji said while talking to TOI.Explaining the reasoning behind seeking a transition in captaincy, Edulji said, "All I'm saying is that Harman is already in her late 30s (37). When would you want her to give up the captaincy and give it to Smriti, who has just entered her 30s (30). I don't want Harman to be dropped from the Indian team. I've no ill-feeling towards her. She's still a great player, but I think Harman should be relieved of the captaincy pressure, and left to just concentrate on her batting, because runs aren't coming off her bat. Harman's form is crucial for our team to win more championships. This move will increase her time span in the India XI. It's very important that someone scores runs in the middle order, because we can't keep depending on our openers all the time. So, I think that this is the right time for Smriti to take over the India captaincy. Her confidence and skill level are high right now. And let Smriti take it forward from here, so that she has a long run (as a captain) then. At least give her white-ball captaincy for now, and maybe Harman can continue as a Test captain.""After a few years, Smriti will be in her late 30s; then what do we do? Whom do we train after that (for India captaincy)? Right now, we can have Jemimah (Rodrigues) or Shafali (Varma) as the vice-captain, and train them (for the bigger responsibility)," Edulji said."Well deserved, Smriti! I’ve watched you grow from a young player into one of the finest batters India has produced. To see you go past my record and become the highest run-scorer in international cricket is a moment I’m genuinely proud of. Here’s to many more runs and milestones. Keep going!," posted Mithali on 'X' on Thursday.Under the 37-year-old Harmanpreet’s captaincy, the Women-in-Blue clinched their maiden ODI World Cup win last year, but exited in the group stage of the Women’s T20 World Cup for the second time in a row. However, they bounced back to beat England by 270 runs in the historic one-off Test at Lord’s. The national selectors have shown faith in Harmanpreet by retaining her as India’s captain for the ongoing Asia Cup in Dubai and the Asian Games in Japan in Sept.In an exclusive interview with TOI on July 14, Mandhana, when asked about whether she was ready for the India captaincy, replied by saying, “Yes, of course, I am ready!”After India’s league stage exit in the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup, India's head coach Amol Muzumdar was asked about Harmanpreet's future, and he said he would like to see her continue as skipper. “It's up to the selectors to decide the captain. I think, yes, my short and sweet answer would be yes,” Muzumdar had stated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sanju Samson-Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to open? Ex-India cricketer suggests new opening combination
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sanju Samson is back in India’s T20I squad for the upcoming series against Afghanistan, giving the wicketkeeper-batter another chance to reclaim his p.
articles.body: Sanju Samson is back in India’s T20I squad for the upcoming series against Afghanistan, giving the wicketkeeper-batter another chance to reclaim his place at the top of the order.Samson was left out of the squad for the Zimbabwe tour after being dropped from the playing XI following three failures. His omission came despite being named Player of the Tournament during India’s T20 World Cup campaign earlier this year.Since India’s World Cup triumph, the team management has continued to experiment with its batting combinations, particularly in the opening slot. Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was fast-tracked into the senior side after a remarkable IPL season and has already been given opportunities to open alongside Abhishek Sharma.With Samson now returning, former India wicketkeeper Deep Dasgupta believes the Afghanistan series could be an opportunity to test another combination, with Samson and Sooryavanshi yet to open together for India.‘We haven’t seen the Sanju-Vaibhav combination yet’Dasgupta pointed out that India have already tried Samson alongside Abhishek Sharma and Sooryavanshi alongside Abhishek, but have not yet seen what Samson and the teenage batter can produce together at the top.“Straight away, if you think about the last match (England T20Is), it was Sanju and Abhishek. Leave Zimbabwe aside. When all three were available, Sanju and Abhishek were there. I think we haven’t seen the Sanju-Vaibhav combination yet. So far, we’ve seen Abhishek-Vaibhav and Abhishek-Sanju, right? It’s not a bad idea to even try and see what kind of combination Sanju and Vaibhav can make,” Dasgupta said on his YouTube channel.Sooryavanshi strengthens case for opening spotSooryavanshi has given the selectors another reason to consider him as a regular option at the top after an impressive series against Zimbabwe.The 15-year-old finished as the leading run-scorer with 151 runs in three innings, averaging 50.33 and striking at 196.10. His performances included a match-winning 81 and two half-centuries, earning him the Player of the Series award.His contribution also played a role in India securing their first series victory under newly appointed T20I captain Shreyas Iyer. India had previously suffered series defeats against Ireland and England.Dasgupta doesn't want Abhishek to be droppedWhile advocating for a possible Samson-Sooryavanshi combination, Dasgupta stressed that he was not calling for any of the three players to be left out.Instead, he wants India to use the matches leading into the T20 World Cup to assess different combinations and ensure players get sufficient opportunities before the final decision is made.“Again, I’m not saying, please don’t get me wrong, I’m not talking about dropping anyone here. I’m just saying, reiterating again, that the idea is that before the World Cup, you want to give every combination and every individual a proper chance and proper game time to understand what works,” he added.With Samson back and Sooryavanshi making a strong case for himself, India’s opening combination is likely to remain one of the key talking points during the Afghanistan series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Too many matches': BCCI admits packed schedule is a challenge, plans better FTP
articles.summary: Cricket News: The BCCI will look to ensure Indian cricketers get enough rest, time to acclimatise and practice matches before major series in SENA countries, secret.
articles.body: The BCCI will look to ensure Indian cricketers get enough rest, time to acclimatise and practice matches before major series in SENA countries, secretary Devajit Saikia said on Thursday.Saikia was speaking after a review meeting at the BCCI headquarters, which discussed India's recent performances and the team's plans for the next year.He said there was no communication gap within Indian cricket on injury management, but acknowledged that the Future Tours Programme (FTP) could be planned better to give players more time to prepare.“Everybody is on the same page. BCCI is working in a very well like a well oiled engine," Saikia told reporters."There is proper coordination amongst all the wings of BCCI, whether it is women's teams committees or their technical staff or their coaches, vis-a-vis the COE, vis-a-vis the Indian men's team’s coaching staff and the head coach. There is no difficulty in the coordination, everything is moving in the right direction.”Saikia said the number of matches being played in a year remains the main challenge for the board.“The only challenge which we are facing is that there are too many matches in the year and that is why in the next FTP we will do certain things, we will take certain measures.“We have instructed our FTP persons who will be meeting very soon in various international forums that our FTP should be in such a way it should be scheduled that there is proper rest for the players as well as some kind of acclimatisation or some kind of friendly matches before any major series in SENA countries (South Africa, Australia, England and New Zealand),” Saikia added.The meeting was attended by India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, head coach Gautam Gambhir, director of cricket at the Centre of Excellence VVS Laxman and other BCCI officials. Selection committee chairman Ajit Agarkar could not join the meeting, even through video conferencing.Saikia said the meeting covered India's performances in England and Ireland and the team's plans for the next year.“We discussed (about) our team performed in England and Ireland and also about what we are going to do about the next one year. The road map has been prepared and we will be doing some exercises so that we have a very good performance in 2027 (ODI) World Cup,” Saikia added.He also acknowledged that India had not done well on their limited-overs tours of Ireland and England. Saikia said the team needed to do some “soul searching”, while adding that a strategy had been “chalked out” in that regard.India lost the two-match T20I series against Ireland 0-2 before losing the T20I series against England 1-4 and the three-match ODI series 1-2.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'They change their mind like pants': Former Pakistan coach tears into chief selector Aaqib Javed over England chaos
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Pakistan head coach Jason Gillespie criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chief selector Aaqib Javed after the board's major mid-series squad.
articles.body: Former Pakistan head coach Jason Gillespie criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chief selector Aaqib Javed after the board's major mid-series squad overhaul following Pakistan's defeats in the first two Tests against England.Pakistan replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, while also sending seven players home after losing the first two Tests at Headingley and Lord's.Gillespie, who coached Pakistan for eight months in 2024 and guided the team to a 2-1 Test series win over England, said it was painful to watch the current situation unfold."I feel for the players, this is these guys livelihoods," Gillespie told The Australian newspaper."From the outside it looks like they are playing with fear," the former Australian fast bowler said."Salman Ali Agha goes from captaining the team in the first Test against England to out of the team for the second Test and on the plane home before the third Test.""How does that work?"The former Australia fast bowler blamed Aaqib Javed for the lack of consistency in Pakistan's selection decisions."It's pretty clear they don't have a selection strategy at all, particularly under Aaqib Javed. They change their mind like they change their pants -- daily," Gillespie said.He also responded to Javed's recent comments, in which the selector blamed Gillespie and former Pakistan white-ball coach Gary Kirsten for the team's problems."Aaqib Javed came out recently and blamed (former Pakistan white-ball coach) Gary Kirsten and myself for everything that is going on."Aaqib has been chairman of selectors for the past two years. We haven't even been there. Somehow he claims it is our fault. Make sense out of that. I think Javed needs to look at himself in the mirror."Gillespie also questioned how the PCB informed players about the squad changes."There is definitely no communication between Aaqib Javed, who is meant to be chairman of selectors, and the players.""The players who were sacked heard it through family and friends and the media they had been sacked. How disrespectful is that?"Reports earlier this week said several Pakistan players found out they had been dropped after friends and family sent them the PCB's statement on social media, with no direct communication from the team management, captain or coach.Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run defeat in the first Test at Headingley before losing the second Test at Lord's by 194 runs, handing England a 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Following those defeats, the PCB recalled wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan, opener Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, spinner Ali Usman, pacer Khurram Shahzad, all-rounder Aamir Jamal and batter Awais Zafar.Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also replaced, with Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke taking charge of the team for the third Test in Birmingham, starting on September 9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: A major age-fraud crackdown has hit Bengal cricket, with the BCCI suspending leg-spinner Rohit Yadav from domestic cricket for two years after discrepancies were found in his age-related documents.The action comes shortly after Rohit was picked for India's Under-19 assignments against Australia. The youngster had also featured in India's U-19 tour of Sri Lanka in July, where he took six wickets and helped the team secure victory in the final Test.Rohit, who hails from Uttar Pradesh, had recently been part of India’s U-19 tour of Sri Lanka in July. He claimed six wickets on the tour and played a key role in India’s victory in the final Test. The spinner was subsequently selected for India’s U-19 home assignments against Australia, with multi-day and one-day matches scheduled to be played in Rajkot and Ahmedabad later this month. However, his selection came under scrutiny after inconsistencies were found in his age-related documents during the Sri Lanka tour.According to the PTI report, Rohit has three birth certificates that list different years of birth - 2007, 2009 and 2010. The discrepancies make him ineligible for age-group cricket and prompted further verification of his records.The 19-year-old, who has represented Bengal in age-group cricket, was found to have an age discrepancy of 27 months, according to the CAB. The ban is effective immediately, with all BCCI-affiliated state associations notified of the decision.CAB flags 62 players over documentation issuesRohit's case is part of a much wider crackdown by the CAB on age and documentation irregularities. The association has declared 62 players ineligible for registration or transfer for competitions during the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons.The CAB has also barred 62 other players over similar age discrepancies. Among them is former India Under-19 World Cup-winning pacer Ravi Kumar, who played a key role in India's title-winning campaign in the 2022 edition in the Caribbean.Ravi, a left-arm pacer, made his senior debut for Bengal in 2022 but last featured for the state in 2023. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Japan are set to share a historic cricketing moment when their men’s sides meet in a T20 International at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture on September 22, 2026, as part of celebrations leading into the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.The Suzuki Cup will mark the first senior-level international cricket match between India and Japan and is being positioned as a significant milestone in the expansion of the sport in Japan. The fixture will also launch “Sport 75”, an initiative aimed at promoting people-to-people exchanges and cooperation between India and Japan through sport. Japan and India will formally mark 75 years of diplomatic relations in 2027.A landmark moment for cricket in JapanThe initiative stems from an agreement reached during a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It also takes into account India’s ambition to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games in 2036.For Japan, the occasion represents an opportunity to showcase the sport to a wider domestic audience, while India’s participation could provide a major boost to cricket’s profile in the country and across East Asia.BCCI honorary secretary Devajit Saikia described the fixture as a “historic occasion” and said the board was delighted to be part of an event that would take Indian cricket into “new territory”.“This is a significant moment for cricket, as it takes the Indian team to new territory and provides an opportunity to introduce the sport to a wider audience in Japan and East Asia,” Saikia said.He also underlined the broader significance of the partnership, saying, “India and Japan share a strong and longstanding relationship and friendship, and we are pleased that cricket will be part of the celebrations marking 75 years of bilateral relations between the two countries.”Saikia added that the BCCI recognised its responsibility to help cricket expand beyond its traditional territories.“The BCCI believes that the growth of cricket must extend beyond its traditional territories, and as the world’s largest cricket board, we recognise our responsibility to contribute to that growth,” he said.Japan ready to welcome IndiaJapan Cricket Association CEO Naoki Miyaji said hosting India, the reigning world champions, represented a landmark occasion for the association.“To be able to invite the reigning World Champions to the home of cricket in Japan is a landmark moment for our association,” Miyaji said.He thanked the BCCI for helping make the fixture possible and said the JCA was looking forward to the response from Indian supporters.“We greatly look forward to welcoming the passion of Indian cricket fans, and we actively encourage any local Japanese people curious about cricket to come and cheer on our team in what will be a truly memorable occasion,” Miyaji said.The articles.title: Pakistan players used to 'chaos' - interim head coach Mike Hesson
articles.summary: Interim Pakistan coach Mike Hesson says his players are used to “chaos” after the tourists dropped seven players and called up seven others for the final Test against England.
articles.body:
Interim Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson said his players are used to "chaos" after the tourists dropped seven players and called up seven others for the final Test against England.

Pakistan have been woeful in losing the first two Tests, and responded by making sweeping changes to the squad as well as replacing head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with New Zealander Hesson.

Hesson, Pakistan's white-ball coach, had recently been in Japan preparing for the Asian Games and was only due to travel to the UK for the squad's audience with King Charles, which took place on Wednesday.

Now, Hesson has been placed in charge of the Test team on a temporary basis for the third Test at Edgbaston, beginning on Wednesday, 9 September (11:00 BST).

"I was heading over to see the King and be part of a nice occasion," said Hesson. "That got expedited.

"The last couple of days have been challenging for being in a hotel with some players coming, some players going and then the arrival of everyone.

"The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. There's no doubt they have been disappointed, incredibly disappointed.

"We've had to park that and go 'righto, where to from here?' They've been really good over the past couple of days."

Hesson was able to explain the process for the squad changes. The three most senior players dropped – batters Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, along with wicketkeeper Muhammad Rizwan – were removed from the party before the former New Zealand coach took over.

Hesson said he then looked at the bowling attack and made changes based on what he believed is required for the conditions at Edgbaston.

Spinner Ali Usman and seamer Khurram Shahzad have both been released after playing in the first two Tests. Neither Aamir Jamal nor Muhammad Awais Jafar have featured on the tour, yet have still been let go.

Into the squad have come batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, both possessing previous Test experience.

Five uncapped players have also been called up: spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah.

"When I took over, three players had already left the squad – Rizwan, Imam and Salman Ali Agha," said Hesson. "From there it was a matter of trying to get a balanced squad for the third Test.

"I don't think anyone wants these to happen in the middle of a series, clearly not.

"From my perspective, it's about putting a balanced squad together, not only for this Test, so we actually have some variety in our attack.

"Pakistan is known for the pace, unusual actions, mystery spin – we haven't really been able to present any of that."

On Friday, Pakistan trained at the indoor centre at Edgbaston because of wet weather in Birmingham. Four of the new arrivals trained with the squad, with three more due to link up later in the day.

Pakistan drop seven players and release head coach

Pakistan changes 'most shocking ever' - Afridi

Hesson also hit back at reports that Salman refused to attend the meeting with King Charles after being dropped.

Salman, Pakistan's T20 captain under Hesson, led the Test side in the series opener at Headingley because of an injury to Babar Azam, then was left out of the XI for the second Test before being omitted from the squad entirely.

Hesson said Salman did not attend the audience with the King because he was part of the trio of players dropped from the squad first and, as a result, Salman, Imam and Rizwan were taken from the list of attendees to Clarence House.

A Pakistan official then confirmed that the four players dropped after Hesson's arrival were still able to meet the King.

"I know there's been a void in news, but people are just making up stories," said Hesson.

"Three players were released from the squad before I arrived and well before [meeting the King]. They were sent a note at the time that these three players will not be attending.

"Someone has just made something up. All of the rest of the players in the squad were already on the list. I was on the list as the white-ball head coach. There has been no changes to it.

"Someone has put two and two together and come up with nine. For me, that's unacceptable journalism."

articles.title: Pakistan coach Mike Hesson breaks silence on mid-England series shake-up, says 'I really don’t know what happened'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s interim red-ball coach Mike Hesson has distanced himself from the decision to release seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third .
articles.body: Pakistan’s interim red-ball coach Mike Hesson has distanced himself from the decision to release seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third and final Test against England, saying three senior players had already been sent home before he was asked to take charge.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) made sweeping changes after the visitors suffered heavy defeats in the first two Tests. England won the series opener by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley before securing a 194-run victory at Lord’s to take an unassailable 2-0 lead.Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were released from the squad, while head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul were also relieved of their duties. Hesson was subsequently handed charge of the Test side for the Edgbaston clash, starting September 9.Hesson clears air on Rizwan, Agha and ImamSpeaking to the media in Birmingham on Friday, Hesson said he had no role in the decision to release Rizwan, Agha and Imam, insisting that the trio had already left the squad when he was approached to manage the Test team.“When they (Pakistan Cricket Board) told me if I could manage the side for the final Test, these three players (Rizwan, Agha and Imam) were already released from the squad and (were) on their way home. So, I really don't know what happened there,” Hesson said.While making it clear that he was not involved in the decision concerning the three senior players, Hesson acknowledged that he did have a role in reshaping the rest of the squad.“I was involved in the release of the rest of the players and the inclusion of some new players,” he said.Hesson explained that he had recently returned from Japan after his involvement with Pakistan’s white-ball setup when the PCB asked him to take over the red-ball side.“We already had a white-ball camp in Lahore and I had just returned from Japan where the Asian Games are taking place, when I was asked if I could manage the red-ball squad,” he added.Hesson wants more variety in bowling attackWith Pakistan already out of contention for the Test series, Hesson said his priority was to create a more balanced squad for the final match.“I decided to make some changes in the squad to get balance into the squad and my emphasis has been on having a bowling attack which has variety and where we have a couple of bowling all-rounders,” he said.The revamped squad includes Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal, along with uncapped players Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran and Razaullah.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Somerset thump Glamorgan to maintain title hopes
articles.summary: Somerset go top of the Division One table in the County Championship with an innings and 64 run victory over Glamorgan.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, The Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton (day three)

Glamorgan 194 & 183: Tribe 49; Overton 3-29

Somerset (23 pts) beat Glamorgan (3 pts) by an innings & 64 runs

Jack Leach, Craig Overton and Lewis Gregory shared nine wickets as Somerset stepped up their challenge for a first ever County Championship title with victory by an innings and 64 runs over Glamorgan inside three days at the Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton.

Left-arm spinner Leach finished with 3-46 and seamers Overton and Gregory 3-29 and 3-68 respectively to restrict the visitors of 183 all out in their second innings from an overnight 30-1. Asa Tribe top scored with 49, while Sean Dickson made 47, but the Welsh county were comprehensively outplayed in all department.

Somerset took 23 points from the game to heap pressure on rivals Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire in what is building towards the most thrilling finale to the title race in years.

Glamorgan had to settle for three points and their challenge appears to be petering out.

The hosts did not have to wait long for a breakthrough when play began five minutes late because of a shower. With 12 runs added to the Glamorgan total, skipper Kiran Carlson nicked a forward defensive push off Migael Pretorius to wicketkeeper James Rew and departed for a duck.

It was 65-3 when Ben Kellaway, on six, got a thicker edge to Overton and presented a waist-high catch to Gregory at third slip.

Colin Ingram survived a run-out scare when Leach missed the stumps at the bowler's end from mid-on with the Glamorgan player short of his ground attempting a quick single.

But there was no stopping Somerset as Leach turned a ball sufficiently from the River End to find the edge of Tribe's bat and Overton pouched the chance at first slip. The opener had faced 108 balls and hit eight fours.

Ingram was next to go, feathering a defensive shot off Overton through to Rew and at 81-5 Glamorgan required a further 166 runs to avoid an innings defeat.

Much rested on the experienced partnership of former Somerset player Dickson and Chris Cooke. By lunch, they had added 30, not without alarm as Leach began to extract regular turn. Dickson was unbeaten on 20 and Cooke nine.

The afternoon session saw the Glamorgan sixth-wicket pair extend their stand beyond the half-century mark as Dickson reverse-swept a boundary off Leach and followed up with a pulled four in the same over.

But, having fought his way to 20 off 46 balls, Cooke was tempted to hook a short ball from Overton and directed the ball into the safe hands of Josh Thomas at fine leg to make it 143-6. With only five added, Dan Douthwaite fell for a first ball duck, lbw to a delivery from Leach that pitched on leg stump from around the wicket and turned sharply.

Dickson's 74-ball resistance ended when he aimed to cut a wide ball from Gregory and Tom Abell took a smart catch two-handed above his head at second slip. With the scoreboard reading 150-8, Somerset's work was almost done.

Gregory found a way through Connor O'Riordan's defences to bowl him for the third duck of the innings and the match ended at 14:40 BST when the Somerset skipper had Timm van der Gugten caught at cover.

Glamorgan coach Richard Dawson told BBC Sport Wales:

"It was a tough two and a half days against a good side high in confidence.

"They put us under pressure from the first morning and we struggled to get back into it.

"We started showing some confidence with individual performances - Asa Tribe played well, Sean Dickson and Ben Kellaway in the first innings. We showed snippets and we hung in there with the ball but realistically Somerset outplayed us."

Report supplied by ECB Reporters' Network, supported by Rothesay.

articles.title: England cricket squads: Aneurin Donald and Henry Crocombe called up for Sri Lanka series
articles.summary: England name the uncapped Aneurin Donald and Henry Crocombe in their squads for the white-ball series against Sri Lanka.
articles.body:
England have named the uncapped Aneurin Donald and Henry Crocombe in their squads for the white-ball series against Sri Lanka.

Derbyshire opener Donald has been included in the 16-player squad for the three-match T20 series, while Sussex seamer Crocombe makes the 16-man line-up for the three one-day internationals.

Donald scored 489 runs in 12 matches captaining Derbyshire Falcons in the Vitality Blast and hit the most sixes in this year's competition with 37.

He also helped Trent Rockets to the final of the Hundred, which the 29-year-old's side lost to Manchester Super Giants.

Crocombe, 24, has taken hat-tricks in his past two County Championship matches and has three five-wicket hauls this season.

England men's national selector Marcus North said the pair are "two promising players who have earned their places on the back of impressive performances in domestic cricket".

He added: "Aneurin has had an exceptional season for Derbyshire in the Vitality Blast and also with Trent Rockets in The Hundred while Henry is a player we have had an eye on all summer."

Meanwhile England all-rounder Jacob Bethell will again be absent after he "underwent successful surgery on his injured knee earlier this week".

He is targeting the white-ball series against Australia in November for his comeback.

Bethell sustained his injury in the ODI series against India in the summer and missed the Test series against Pakistan.

He is also expected to be absent for an ODI tri-series against hosts Pakistan and Sri Lanka in Lahore and Rawalpindi in October.

Batter Phil Salt is unavailable because of a right quad injury, while bowler Jamie Overton is in both squads after missing the white-ball series against India earlier with a thigh injury.

Durham seamer Brydon Carse has not been included in either squad to face Sri Lanka.

The 31-year-old was dropped for the second Test of the current series against Pakistan after he was briefly arrested following an incident outside a Derby nightclub on 22 August.

Derbyshire police are continuing to investigate an allegation of assault in connection with that incident.

"Whiile Brydon was available for selection, he has not been picked for the Sri Lanka series squad," said the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB).

"Given recent events, we feel it is important for him to work through the issues that led to the Derby incident and take time for a proper reset. This decision does not prejudge the outcome of any investigation."

There are not expected to be any updates from the police imminently, while the Cricket Regulator will wait until that investigation is completed before looking into the incident.

articles.title: Lhuan-dre-Pretorius’ 101, Connor Esterhuizen’s 88 help South Africa survive Namibia scare to reach final
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa held their nerve in a thrilling high-scoring contest against Namibia, securing an 11-run victory at the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoe.
articles.body: South Africa held their nerve in a thrilling high-scoring contest against Namibia, securing an 11-run victory at the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek on Friday to book their place in the Namibia T20I Tri-Series final.After posting a mammoth 228/4 in 20 overs, South Africa were pushed all the way by the hosts, who finished on 217/3 despite a spirited chase. The result means South Africa will face Zimbabwe in the final on Sunday.Pretorius, Esterhuizen power South Africa to 228South Africa's innings was dominated by a spectacular opening partnership between Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Connor Esterhuizen. Esterhuizen smashed 88 off just 40 balls, clearing the ropes eight times and hitting six fours, while Pretorius produced the innings of the day with a magnificent 101 off 53 balls, including five fours and eight sixes. Their opening stand was worth 156 runs and laid the foundation for a daunting total.Pretorius reached his maiden T20I century in the final over, completing the landmark in 52 deliveries. His hundred came only days after he had narrowly missed out against Zimbabwe with a career-best 94.South Africa eventually finished on 228/4, setting Namibia a required run rate of 11.45 an over.Namibia launch stunning fightbackNamibia refused to surrender despite the enormous target. Openers Louren Steenkamp and Jan Frylinck gave the hosts exactly the start they needed, keeping pace with the asking rate and putting South Africa under pressure.Frylinck produced a sensational 72 off 36 balls, while Steenkamp contributed a composed 61 off 44, ensuring Namibia remained firmly in the contest for much of the chase. Namibia crossed 200 with the game still alive, leaving South Africa facing a tense finish.The final overs belonged to South Africa's bowlers as they finally managed to squeeze the boundaries out of Namibia.With the hosts needing a huge finish, Nqobani Mokoena delivered the decisive blow in the final over. He dismissed Ruben Trumpelmann caught behind, with Connor Esterhuizen completing the catch, as Namibia ended on 217/3 after 19.6 overs.The result also confirmed the final line-up: South Africa will meet Zimbabwe in Sunday's final, while Namibia's impressive campaign ends with a narrow defeat despite their remarkable 217-run chase.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women’s Asia Cup: ‘Focus on cricket, not the noise,’ Mithali Raj tells India ahead of Pakistan clash
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: With a 137-run win over Hong Kong, India sealed their place in the Women’s Asia Cup semifinals with a match to spare. Their final league ou.
articles.body: BENGALURU: With a 137-run win over Hong Kong, India sealed their place in the Women’s Asia Cup semifinals with a match to spare. Their final league outing, however, will be their toughest test yet after they brushed aside minnows Thailand and Hong Kong in their opening two games.On Saturday in Dubai, Harmanpreet Kaur and her team take on cross-border rivals Pakistan in what could serve as a dress rehearsal ahead of next week’s semifinal.With India’s middle order still a concern, former India captain Mithali Raj has urged the team to focus on cricket rather than get consumed by the noise surrounding the rivalry.“You prepare for the cricket, not the noise. Understand your role, anticipate what the opposition may do and know how you will respond. We cannot control what people say outside, but we can control our preparation, communication and reaction under pressure. Clarity of role makes it easier to block out the noise,” the former star batter told TOI.India have dominated Pakistan in T20 cricket, winning 17 of their 20 meetings, but Mithali believes the numbers matter little once the two sides walk out.“It’s an emotional and traditional rivalry. The India vs Pakistan game means a lot to each player. Winning this game is a matter of pride and therefore, the added pressure on the team to perform,” she said.Sending a message to the Indian team, the 43-year-old added: “For the players, it is a cricket match after all, and it’s important to keep calm to do well on the ground. If you focus too much on what it means outside the boundary, you create unnecessary pressure. The atmosphere and expectations will be different, but once you cross the boundary, you have to focus on your role and the team’s plans. I believe India, of course, are the favourites to win the match.”Mithali also believes the Asia Cup should be viewed as more than just preparation for the upcoming Asian Games, where India will defend the gold medal they won on their debut in the previous edition.“Having lost the last edition of the Asia Cup, India will be looking to reclaim the title. I don’t think they will necessarily look at this tournament only as preparation for the Asian Games,” she pointed out.For the developing teams in the competition, Mithali feels the tournament offers an important platform to measure their progress against the best.“The Asia Cup allows developing sides to test themselves against the best. The gap in experience and resources still exists, but it is narrowing. With cricket now an Olympic sport and also part of the Asian Games, teams have more platforms to compete.”“If you look at the recent two World Cups across different formats, teams like Pakistan and Bangladesh have shown that they can put the top teams under pressure. Tournaments like the Asia Cup are also a good indicator of how much the game has developed across different countries,” Mithali explained.(Watch ACC Women's Asia Cup 2026 on Sony Sports Ten 1 SD & HD and Sony LIV)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England call up Henry Crocombe and Aneurin Donald for white-ball series against Sri Lanka but no Brydon Carse
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell, Sam Curran and Phil Salt injured, while no place for Brydon Carse in T20 or ODI squads; England face Sri Lanka in three T20s and three ODIs; watch the first T20, in Southampton, live on Sky Sports on Tuesday September 15 (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
Donald plundered 489 runs, including four half-centuries, across 12 matches in this summer's Vitality Blast - he also hit the most sixes with 37 - while he then impressed for Trent Rockets in The Hundred.

The Wales-born player - who struck the joint-fastest Blast fifty, off just 13 balls, for Derbyshire against Yorkshire in 2025 - comes into a 16-man T20 squad missing opening batter Phil Salt (quad).

Crocombe, who has taken hat-tricks in his last two County Championship matches, is part of a 16-strong ODI group.

Brydon Carse, currently being investigated by the Cricket Regulator after an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August, is not included for the ODIs or T20s, having already been withdrawn from recent Test squads to face Pakistan.

Sam Curran (groin) and Jacob Bethell (knee) are absent through injury - the ECB has said Bethell underwent successful surgery this week and is targeting the white-ball tour of Australia in November as a return date.

Curran and Bethell's fellow all-rounder Jamie Overton returns after sitting out the T20 and ODI series victories at home to India in July with a quad issue sustained at the IPL, while batters Jordan Cox and Ben Duckett are in both squads.

The T20 leg versus Sri Lanka begins in Southampton on September 15 - two days after the scheduled end of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston - ahead of games in Cardiff on September 17 and Emirates Old Trafford on September 19.

The ODIs, England's final assignment of the home summer, then take place at Durham (September 22), Headingley (September 24) and The Kia Oval (September 27).

Chance for Crocombe and Coles to impress?

Crocombe was added to England's Test party during the New Zealand series in June when Sussex team-mate Ollie Robinson picked up a knee niggle but did not feature.

The 24-year-old, who will join Surrey from 2027 onwards, has claimed 49 wickets across 36 domestic 50-over matches and a further 34 in 35 T20 fixtures, with those numbers adding to over 100 scalps in red-ball cricket.

Crocombe's recent first-class hat-tricks came against Somerset and Essex, with his victims including Jamie Overton's twin brother Craig.

Another uncapped Sussex player, spin-bowling all-rounder James Coles, retains his place in the ODI and T20 groups after earning a maiden call-up for the India games a couple of months ago.

T20 call-up Donald has hit 18 fifties in that format domestically across 106 innings, with a best of 91.

Brendon McCullum - now solely white-ball coach after his removal from the Test job following the 2-1 defeat to New Zealand - can call upon Test captain Joe Root for the ODIs with England opting against resting him.

Before tackling Sri Lanka, England will look to complete a 3-0 Test sweep of Pakistan in Birmingham from September 9, also live on Sky Sports, after thumping wins across the first two games at Headingley and Lord's.

England head to Pakistan in October for an ODI tri-series that also features Sri Lanka, prior to visiting Australia in November for three one-day internationals and five T20s.

The three-Test tour of South Africa over the Christmas period - Stephen Fleming's first as red-ball coach since succeeding McCullum in the role - will be followed by three ODIs against the Proteas in January.

The next 50-over World Cup is in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in late 2027, before a T20 World Cup is held in Australia and New Zealand the following year.

articles.title: Mohsin Naqvi gets a fresh roast: Iceland Cricket offers ‘all expenses paid’ trip to ‘learn selection strategy’ from PCB chief
articles.summary: Iceland Cricket cheekily took aim at Pakistan Cricket Board chairman Mohsin Naqvi by suggesting a bold challenge: clearing an iceberg for an adventurous trip...
articles.body:
Iceland Cricket has taken a cheeky swipe at Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi, using an imaginary cricketing challenge to mock the board's recent selection decisions and the growing criticism surrounding its administration. The Iceland Cricket account, known for its humorous and often sarcastic posts on X, took aim at Naqvi amid a turbulent period for Pakistan cricket. The post appeared to reference the PCB's controversial decisions during the ongoing Test series against England, as well as Naqvi's recent comments while defending the board's actions. "We are going to launch a new cricketing challenge for coastal cricketers. Clear an iceberg and you win an all-expenses paid educational trip to meet Mohsin Naqvi and learn about selection strategy. Trip can be one-way if you wish," Iceland Cricket wrote on X.

The joke comes days after Pakistan made a dramatic overhaul of their Test squad following two heavy defeats against England. The PCB released seven players from the tour and replaced head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed ahead of the third Test, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson taking charge of the red-ball side. Bowling coach Umar Gul was also replaced by Ashley Noffke. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were among those released from the squad after Pakistan went 2-0 down in the three-match series. Earlier, following Pakistan's defeat at Lord's, the team attended a dinner with King Charles. Iceland Cricket also took a dig at the PCB and the Pakistan team over the visit, joking: "You can bet he didn't know who most of the players were, because nobody else does"

Naqvi's India-Ireland remark draws attention

Naqvi has also faced criticism over his response to questions surrounding Pakistan's performances and the PCB's decisions. While defending the changes, the PCB chairman pointed to India's recent T20I defeat against Ireland and questioned whether that meant "cricket had ended". His comments were intended to argue that even leading teams can suffer unexpected defeats and that Pakistan's setbacks should not be viewed as the end of the country's cricketing fortunes.
